   323→    def _sync_solaris_viewport(self, memory_path: str) -> None:
   324→        """
   325→        R10: Ensures Houdini's live scene graph syncs with evolved memory.
   326→
   327→        After evolution writes a new memory.usd, any LOP node that references
   328→        this file (via sublayer or reference) will be stale. This method
   329→        finds those nodes and force-cooks them so the Solaris viewport
   330→        immediately reflects the evolved data.
   331→
   332→        H21: hou.lopNetworks() was removed. We walk the node tree from root
   333→        and collect hou.LopNetwork instances instead.
   334→        """
   335→        if not _HOU_AVAILABLE:
   336→            return
   337→
   338→        try:
   339→            # H21: find LOP networks by walking the node tree
   340→            lop_networks = []
   341→            stack = [hou.node("/")]
   342→            while stack:
   343→                n = stack.pop()
   344→                if isinstance(n, hou.LopNetwork):
   345→                    lop_networks.append(n)
   346→                try:
   347→                    stack.extend(n.children())
   348→                except Exception:
   349→                    pass
   350→
   351→            for lop_net in lop_networks:
   352→                for node in lop_net.children():
   353→                    if node.type().name() in ("sublayer", "reference"):
   354→                        file_parm = node.parm("filepath1")
   355→                        if file_parm and memory_path in file_parm.evalAsString():
   356→                            node.cook(force=True)
   357→        except Exception:
   358→            pass  # Viewport sync is best-effort, never blocks evolution

   360→    # ── R3: Native OpenUSD Generation ────────────────────────
   361→
   362→    def _build_usd_native(self, parsed: ParsedMemory) -> str:
   363→        """
   364→        R3: Native pxr.Usd generation. Eliminates ALL string-template bugs:
   365→          - Tf.MakeValidIdentifier() ensures safe prim names
   366→          - Vt.StringArray() handles arrays without manual quoting
   367→          - Native String attributes auto-escape VEX slashes, quotes, linebreaks
   368→          - ExportToString() produces syntactically perfect USDA
   369→        """
   370→        stage = Usd.Stage.CreateInMemory()
   371→
   372→        root_prim = stage.DefinePrim("/SYNAPSE", "Xform")
   373→        stage.SetDefaultPrim(root_prim)
   374→
   375→        # Layer metadata
   376→        stage.GetRootLayer().customLayerData = {
   377→            "synapse:version": "2.0.0-lossless",
   378→            "synapse:evolution_stage": "charmeleon",
   379→            "synapse:evolved_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
   380→            "synapse:session_count": len(parsed.sessions),
   381→            "synapse:decision_count": len(parsed.decisions),
   382→            "synapse:asset_count": len(parsed.assets),
   383→            "synapse:parameter_count": len(parsed.parameters),
   384→        }
   385→
   386→        memory_prim = stage.DefinePrim("/SYNAPSE/memory", "Xform")
   387→
   388→        # ── Sessions ────────────────────────────────────────
   389→        sessions_prim = stage.DefinePrim(f"{memory_prim.GetPath()}/sessions", "Xform")
   390→        for session in parsed.sessions:
   391→            safe_id = Tf.MakeValidIdentifier(session.id)
   392→            sess_prim = stage.DefinePrim(f"{sessions_prim.GetPath()}/{safe_id}", "Xform")
   393→
   394→            sess_prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:date", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(session.date)
   395→            sess_prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:narrative", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(session.text)
   396→
   397→            if session.decisions:
   398→                sess_prim.CreateAttribute(
   399→                    "synapse:decisions", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.StringArray
   400→                ).Set(Vt.StringArray(session.decisions))
   401→            if session.blockers:
   402→                sess_prim.CreateAttribute(
   403→                    "synapse:blockers", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.StringArray
   404→                ).Set(Vt.StringArray(session.blockers))
   405→
   406→        # ── Decisions ───────────────────────────────────────
   407→        decisions_prim = stage.DefinePrim(f"{memory_prim.GetPath()}/decisions", "Xform")
   408→        for decision in parsed.decisions:
   409→            safe_slug = Tf.MakeValidIdentifier(decision.slug)
   410→            d_prim = stage.DefinePrim(f"{decisions_prim.GetPath()}/{safe_slug}", "Xform")
   411→
   412→            d_prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:choice", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(decision.choice)
   413→            d_prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:reasoning", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(decision.reasoning)
   414→            d_prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:date", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(decision.date)
   415→            if decision.alternatives:
   416→                d_prim.CreateAttribute(
   417→                    "synapse:alternatives", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.StringArray
   418→                ).Set(Vt.StringArray(decision.alternatives))
   419→
   420→        # ── Assets ──────────────────────────────────────────
   421→        assets_prim = stage.DefinePrim(f"{memory_prim.GetPath()}/assets", "Xform")
   422→        for asset in parsed.assets:
   423→            safe_name = Tf.MakeValidIdentifier(asset.name)
   424→            a_prim = stage.DefinePrim(f"{assets_prim.GetPath()}/{safe_name}", "Xform")
   425→
   426→            a_prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:path", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Asset).Set(asset.path)
   427→            a_prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:notes", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(asset.notes)
   428→            if asset.variants:
   429→                a_prim.CreateAttribute(
   430→                    "synapse:variants", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.StringArray
   431→                ).Set(Vt.StringArray(asset.variants))
   432→
   433→        # ── Parameters ──────────────────────────────────────
   434→        params_prim = stage.DefinePrim(f"{memory_prim.GetPath()}/parameters", "Xform")
   435→        for param in parsed.parameters:
   436→            safe_slug = Tf.MakeValidIdentifier(param.slug)
   437→            p_prim = stage.DefinePrim(f"{params_prim.GetPath()}/{safe_slug}", "Xform")
   438→
   439→            p_prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:node_path", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(param.node)
   440→            p_prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:parm_name", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(param.name)
   441→            p_prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:before", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(param.before)
   442→            p_prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:after", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(param.after)
   443→            p_prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:result", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(param.result)
   444→            if param.date:
   445→                p_prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:date", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(param.date)
   446→
   447→        # ExportToString produces syntactically perfect USDA
   448→        return stage.GetRootLayer().ExportToString()

   459→            if memory.id in self._memories:
   460→                memory.updated_at = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())

   462→                self._index_memory(memory)
   463→                self._dirty = True

   513→    def search(self, query: MemoryQuery) -> List[MemorySearchResult]:
   514→        """Search memories based on query parameters.
   515→
   516→        Uses the in-memory index to narrow candidates before scoring,
   517→        avoiding a full scan when type/tag/keyword filters are provided.
   518→        Falls back to full scan only for pure text queries.
   519→        """
   520→        self._wait_loaded()
   521→        with self._lock.read_lock():
   522→            # --- Candidate narrowing via index ---
   523→            candidates = None  # None = "all", set() = "none matched yet"
   524→
   525→            if query.memory_types:
   526→                type_ids: set = set()
   527→                for mt in query.memory_types:
   528→                    type_ids.update(self._index["by_type"].get(mt.value, []))
   529→                candidates = type_ids
   530→
   531→            if query.tags:
   532→                tag_ids: set = set()
   533→                for tag in query.tags:
   534→                    tag_ids.update(self._index["by_tag"].get(tag, []))
   535→                candidates = tag_ids if candidates is None else candidates & tag_ids
   536→
   537→            if query.keywords:
   538→                kw_ids: set = set()
   539→                for kw in query.keywords:
   540→                    kw_ids.update(self._index["by_keyword"].get(kw, []))
   541→                candidates = kw_ids if candidates is None else candidates & kw_ids
   542→
   543→            # Resolve candidate IDs to Memory objects
   544→            if candidates is not None:
   545→                pool = [self._memories[mid] for mid in candidates if mid in self._memories]
   546→            else:
   547→                pool = list(self._memories.values())
   548→
   549→            # --- Score candidates ---
   550→            results = []
   551→
   552→            for memory in pool:
   553→                if memory.is_consolidated and not query.include_consolidated:
   554→                    continue
   555→
   556→                # Post-filter: tier, source, time range
   557→                if query.tier and memory.tier != query.tier:
   558→                    continue
   559→                if query.source and memory.source != query.source:
   560→                    continue
   561→                if query.since and memory.created_at < query.since:
   562→                    continue
   563→                if query.until and memory.created_at > query.until:
   564→                    continue
   565→
   566→                score = 0.0
   567→                match_reasons = []
   568→
   569→                # Tag scoring (index already filtered, but score the overlap)
   570→                if query.tags:
   571→                    matching_tags = set(query.tags) & set(memory.tags)
   572→                    if matching_tags:
   573→                        score += len(matching_tags) * 0.2
   574→                        match_reasons.append(f"tags: {', '.join(matching_tags)}")
   575→
   576→                # Keyword scoring
   577→                if query.keywords:
   578→                    matching_keywords = set(query.keywords) & set(memory.keywords)
   579→                    if matching_keywords:
   580→                        score += len(matching_keywords) * 0.2
   581→                        match_reasons.append(f"keywords: {', '.join(matching_keywords)}")
   582→
   583→                # Text search (still linear over candidates, but candidate set is smaller)
   584→                if query.text:
   585→                    text_lower = query.text.lower()
   586→                    content_lower = memory.content.lower()
   587→                    summary_lower = memory.summary.lower()
   588→
   589→                    if text_lower in content_lower:
   590→                        score += 0.5
   591→                        match_reasons.append("content match")
   592→                    if text_lower in summary_lower:
   593→                        score += 0.3
   594→                        match_reasons.append("summary match")
   595→
   596→                    words = text_lower.split()
   597→                    word_matches = sum(1 for w in words if w in content_lower or w in summary_lower)
   598→                    if word_matches > 0:
   599→                        score += word_matches * 0.1
   600→                        match_reasons.append(f"{word_matches} word matches")
   601→
   602→                # No criteria = return all with base score
   603→                if not query.text and not query.tags and not query.keywords:
   604→                    score = 0.5
   605→
   606→                if score > 0:
   607→                    results.append(MemorySearchResult(
   608→                        memory=memory,
   609→                        score=min(1.0, score),
   610→                        match_reasons=match_reasons
   611→                    ))
   612→
   613→            # He2025: stable sort with ID tiebreaker for deterministic ordering
   614→            results.sort(key=lambda r: (-r.score, r.memory.id))
   615→
   616→            if query.limit > 0:
   617→                results = results[:query.limit]
   618→
   619→            return results
   620→

   658→# =============================================================================
   659→# SYNAPSE MEMORY - HIGH-LEVEL API

   661→
   662→class SynapseMemory:
   663→    """
   664→    High-level API for Synapse memory system.
   665→
   666→    Automatically detects current Houdini project and manages memory storage.
   667→    Provides convenient methods for common operations.
   668→
   669→    Migration: Automatically migrates .nexus/ or .engram/ to .synapse/ if needed.
   670→    """
   671→
   672→    def __init__(self, project_path: Optional[str] = None):
   673→        """
   674→        Initialize Synapse for a project.
   675→
   676→        Args:
   677→            project_path: Optional path to .hip file or project directory.
   678→                         If None, uses current Houdini project.
   679→        """
   680→        self.project_path = self._resolve_project_path(project_path)
   681→        self.storage_dir = self._get_storage_dir()
   682→        self.store = MemoryStore(self.storage_dir)
   683→
   684→        # Callbacks
   685→        self._on_memory_added: List[Callable[[Memory], None]] = []
   686→        self._on_memory_updated: List[Callable[[Memory], None]] = []
   687→
   688→        logger.info("Initialized for project: %s", self.project_path)

   690→
   691→    def _resolve_project_path(self, path: Optional[str]) -> Path:
   692→        """Resolve the project path."""
   693→        if path:
   694→            return Path(path)
   695→
   696→        if HOU_AVAILABLE:
   697→            hip_path = hou.hipFile.path()
   698→            if hip_path and hip_path != "untitled.hip":
   699→                return Path(hip_path)
   700→            else:
   701→                # Use temp directory for unsaved projects
   702→                return Path(hou.text.expandString("$HOUDINI_TEMP_DIR")) / "untitled"
   703→
   704→        # Fallback
   705→        return Path.cwd() / "untitled.hip"
   706→
   707→    def _get_storage_dir(self) -> Path:
   708→        """
   709→        Get the storage directory for this project.
   710→
   711→        3-tier migration logic:
   712→        1. If .synapse/ exists -> use it
   713→        2. If .nexus/ exists -> copy to .synapse/, leave marker
   714→        3. If .engram/ exists -> copy to .synapse/, leave marker
   715→        4. Otherwise -> create .synapse/
   716→        """
   717→        if self.project_path.is_file():
   718→            base_dir = self.project_path.parent
   719→        else:
   720→            base_dir = self.project_path
   721→
   722→        synapse_dir = base_dir / ".synapse"
   723→        nexus_dir = base_dir / ".nexus"
   724→        engram_dir = base_dir / ".engram"
   725→
   726→        # Priority 1: Use existing .synapse/
   727→        if synapse_dir.exists():
   728→            return synapse_dir
   729→
   730→        # Priority 2: Migrate from .nexus/
   731→        if nexus_dir.exists():
   732→            try:
   733→                logger.info("Migrating from .nexus/ to .synapse/")
   734→                shutil.copytree(nexus_dir, synapse_dir)
   735→                migration_marker = nexus_dir / ".migrated_to_synapse"
   736→                migration_marker.write_text(
   737→                    f"Migrated to .synapse/ on {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\n"
   738→                    f"This directory is kept for backwards compatibility.\n"
   739→                    f"You can safely delete it."
   740→                )
   741→                logger.info("Migration complete: %s -> %s", nexus_dir, synapse_dir)
   742→                return synapse_dir
   743→            except Exception as e:
   744→                logger.warning("Migration failed: %s. Using .nexus/ directly.", e)
   745→                return nexus_dir
   746→
   747→        # Priority 3: Migrate from .engram/
   748→        if engram_dir.exists():
   749→            try:
   750→                logger.info("Migrating from .engram/ to .synapse/")
   751→                shutil.copytree(engram_dir, synapse_dir)
   752→                migration_marker = engram_dir / ".migrated_to_synapse"
   753→                migration_marker.write_text(
   754→                    f"Migrated to .synapse/ on {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\n"
   755→                    f"This directory is kept for backwards compatibility.\n"
   756→                    f"You can safely delete it."
   757→                )
   758→                logger.info("Migration complete: %s -> %s", engram_dir, synapse_dir)
   759→                return synapse_dir
   760→            except Exception as e:
   761→                logger.warning("Migration failed: %s. Using .engram/ directly.", e)
   762→                return engram_dir
   763→
   764→        # Priority 4: Create new .synapse/
   765→        return synapse_dir

   767→    def add(

   822→

   958→    def _extract_keywords(self, text: str, max_keywords: int = 5) -> List[str]:
   959→        """Simple keyword extraction from text."""
   960→        # Remove common words
   961→        stop_words = {
   962→            'the', 'a', 'an', 'is', 'are', 'was', 'were', 'be', 'been',
   963→            'being', 'have', 'has', 'had', 'do', 'does', 'did', 'will',
   964→            'would', 'could', 'should', 'may', 'might', 'must', 'shall',
   965→            'can', 'need', 'dare', 'ought', 'used', 'to', 'of', 'in',
   966→            'for', 'on', 'with', 'at', 'by', 'from', 'as', 'into',
   967→            'through', 'during', 'before', 'after', 'above', 'below',
   968→            'between', 'under', 'again', 'further', 'then', 'once',
   969→            'and', 'but', 'or', 'nor', 'so', 'yet', 'both', 'either',
   970→            'neither', 'not', 'only', 'same', 'than', 'too', 'very',
   971→            'just', 'also', 'now', 'here', 'there', 'when', 'where',
   972→            'why', 'how', 'all', 'each', 'every', 'both', 'few', 'more',
   973→            'most', 'other', 'some', 'such', 'no', 'any', 'this', 'that',
   974→            'these', 'those', 'what', 'which', 'who', 'whom', 'whose'
   975→        }
   976→
   977→        # Tokenize and filter
   978→        words = text.lower().split()
   979→        words = [w.strip('.,!?;:()[]{}"\'-') for w in words]
   980→        words = [w for w in words if w and len(w) > 2 and w not in stop_words]
   981→
   982→        # Count frequencies
   983→        freq: Dict[str, int] = {}
   984→        for w in words:
   985→            freq[w] = freq.get(w, 0) + 1
   986→
   987→        # Return top keywords
   988→        sorted_words = sorted(freq.items(), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
   989→        return [w for w, _ in sorted_words[:max_keywords]]

   504→def _extract_blockers(content: str) -> List[str]:
   505→    """Extract unresolved blocker sections from markdown memory."""

   537→def _truncate(text: str, max_chars: int) -> str:
   538→    """Truncate text to max_chars, preserving complete lines."""
   539→    if len(text) <= max_chars:
   540→        return text
   541→    truncated = text[:max_chars]
   542→    last_newline = truncated.rfind("\n")
   543→    if last_newline > max_chars // 2:
   544→        truncated = truncated[:last_newline]
   545→    return truncated + "\n...(truncated)"

   548→def _parse_sections(content: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   549→    """Split markdown memory into typed sections.
   550→
   551→    Each section has: type, title, text, line.
   552→    Section types: session, decision, parameter, blocker, blocker_resolved,
   553→    note, wedge, session_end, header.
   554→    """
   555→    import re
   556→
   557→    sections: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   558→    current: Dict[str, Any] = {"type": "header", "title": "", "text": "", "line": 1}
   559→
   560→    _SECTION_PATTERNS = [
   561→        ("## Session ", "session"),
   562→        ("### Decision:", "decision"),
   563→        ("### Parameter:", "parameter"),
   564→        ("### Blocker", None),          # special: resolved vs open
   565→        ("### Note", "note"),
   566→        ("### Wedge", "wedge"),
   567→        ("### Session End", "session_end"),
   568→    ]
   569→
   570→    for i, line in enumerate(content.split("\n"), 1):
   571→        matched = False
   572→        for prefix, sec_type in _SECTION_PATTERNS:
   573→            if not line.startswith(prefix):
   574→                continue
   575→            if current["text"].strip():
   576→                sections.append(current)
   577→
   578→            if prefix == "### Blocker":
   579→                is_resolved = "Resolved" in line
   580→                current = {
   581→                    "type": "blocker_resolved" if is_resolved else "blocker",
   582→                    "title": re.sub(r'^### Blocker\s*(Resolved)?:\s*', '', line).strip(),
   583→                    "text": line + "\n",
   584→                    "line": i,
   585→                }
   586→            elif prefix == "### Decision:":
   587→                current = {
   588→                    "type": "decision",
   589→                    "title": line.replace("### Decision:", "").strip(),
   590→                    "text": line + "\n",
   591→                    "line": i,
   592→                }
   593→            elif prefix == "### Parameter:":
   594→                current = {
   595→                    "type": "parameter",
   596→                    "title": line.replace("### Parameter:", "").strip(),
   597→                    "text": line + "\n",
   598→                    "line": i,
   599→                }
   600→            else:
   601→                current = {
   602→                    "type": sec_type,
   603→                    "title": line.strip("# \n") if sec_type != "session_end" else "Session End",
   604→                    "text": line + "\n",
   605→                    "line": i,
   606→                }
   607→            matched = True
   608→            break
   609→        if not matched:
   610→            current["text"] += line + "\n"
   611→
   612→    if current["text"].strip():
   613→        sections.append(current)
   614→    return sections

   617→def search_memory(content: str, query: str, type_filter: str = "") -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   618→    """
   619→    Section-aware memory search with TF-IDF scoring.
   620→
   621→    Splits markdown into sections, computes TF-IDF for each query term
   622→    across all sections, then ranks by combined score. Rare terms (e.g.
   623→    specific node names) are weighted higher than common ones (e.g. "render").
   624→
   625→    Args:
   626→        content: Raw markdown memory content
   627→        query: Search query string
   628→        type_filter: Optional section type filter (decision, parameter, blocker, session, note)
   629→
   630→    Returns: Sorted list of {section_type, title, text, score, line}
   631→    """
   632→    import math
   633→    import re
   634→
   635→    if not content or not query:
   636→        return []
   637→
   638→    # Tokenize query into lowercase words (2+ chars for relevance)
   639→    query_words = [
   640→        w for w in re.findall(r'[a-z0-9_/]+', query.lower()) if len(w) >= 2
   641→    ]
   642→    query_word_set = set(query_words)
   643→    if not query_word_set:
   644→        return []
   645→
   646→    # Parse sections
   647→    sections = _parse_sections(content)
   648→    if type_filter:
   649→        sections = [s for s in sections if s["type"] == type_filter]
   650→
   651→    # Pre-compute: tokenize each section and build word lists
   652→    scorable = []
   653→    for section in sections:
   654→        if section["type"] == "header":
   655→            continue
   656→        words = re.findall(r'[a-z0-9_/]+', section["text"].lower())
   657→        word_set = set(words)
   658→        if not (query_word_set & word_set):
   659→            continue  # Skip sections with zero overlap
   660→        scorable.append((section, words, word_set))
   661→
   662→    if not scorable:
   663→        return []
   664→
   665→    # IDF: log(N / df) where N = total scorable sections, df = sections containing term
   666→    n_docs = len(scorable)
   667→    doc_freq: Dict[str, int] = {}
   668→    for _, _, word_set in scorable:
   669→        for w in query_word_set:
   670→            if w in word_set:
   671→                doc_freq[w] = doc_freq.get(w, 0) + 1
   672→
   673→    idf: Dict[str, float] = {}
   674→    for w in query_word_set:
   675→        df = doc_freq.get(w, 0)
   676→        # Smoothed IDF: log((N + 1) / (df + 1)) + 1
   677→        idf[w] = math.log((n_docs + 1) / (df + 1)) + 1.0
   678→
   679→    # Score each section with TF-IDF
   680→    results = []
   681→    for section, words, word_set in scorable:
   682→        n_words = len(words) or 1  # avoid /0
   683→
   684→        # TF-IDF sum for matching query terms
   685→        tfidf_score = 0.0
   686→        for w in query_word_set:
   687→            if w not in word_set:
   688→                continue
   689→            tf = words.count(w) / n_words
   690→            tfidf_score += tf * idf[w]
   691→
   692→        # Normalize by number of query terms for comparability
   693→        tfidf_score /= len(query_word_set)
   694→
   695→        # Title boost: query terms in title get 2x IDF weight
   696→        title_words = set(re.findall(r'[a-z0-9_/]+', section["title"].lower()))
   697→        title_matches = query_word_set & title_words
   698→        if title_matches:
   699→            for w in title_matches:
   700→                tfidf_score += idf[w] * 0.5 / len(query_word_set)
   701→
   702→        # Exact phrase bonus
   703→        if query.lower() in section["text"].lower():
   704→            tfidf_score += 0.5
   705→
   706→        results.append({
   707→            "section_type": section["type"],
   708→            "title": section["title"],
   709→            "text": section["text"].strip()[:500],
   710→            "score": round(tfidf_score, 3),
   711→            "line": section["line"],
   712→        })
   713→
   714→    # Sort by score descending, then by line ascending for tiebreaker
   715→    results.sort(key=lambda r: (-r["score"], r["line"]))
   716→    return results
   717→
   718→
   719→def get_evolution_stage(claude_dir: str, name: str = "memory") -> str:
   720→    """Detect current evolution stage: charmander, charmeleon, or charizard."""
   721→    claude_dir = os.path.normpath(claude_dir)

    28→def count_structured_data(md_path: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:

    33→    with open(md_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:

    47→    for line in lines:

   103→def parse_markdown_memory(md_path: str) -> Dict[str, List]:

   118→    parameters: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
   119→
   120→    # Split by ## Session headers
   121→    session_blocks = re.split(r'^## Session ', content, flags=re.MULTILINE)
   122→
   123→    for i, block in enumerate(session_blocks[1:], 1):
   124→        lines = block.strip().split("\n")
   125→        header = lines[0] if lines else ""
   126→        date = header.split()[0] if header else f"session_{i}"
   127→        text = "\n".join(lines)

   129→        session: Dict[str, Any] = {

   137→
   138→        # Extract decisions within this session
   139→        decision_blocks = re.findall(
   140→            r'### Decision:\s*(.+?)(?=\n###|\n## |\Z)',
   141→            text, re.DOTALL
   142→        )
   143→        for db in decision_blocks:
   144→            decision_lines = db.strip().split("\n")

   146→            choice = ""

   156→                "name": name,
   157→                "choice": choice,
   158→                "reasoning": reasoning,
   159→                "date": date,
   160→                "alternatives": [],
   161→            })
   162→            session["decisions"].append(slug)
   163→
   164→        # Extract parameters
   165→        param_blocks = re.findall(
   166→            r'### Parameter:\s*(.+?)(?=\n###|\n## |\Z)',
   167→            text, re.DOTALL
   168→        )
   169→        for pb in param_blocks:
   170→            param_lines = pb.strip().split("\n")
   171→            header_parts = param_lines[0].strip().split("/") if param_lines else []
   172→            before = after = result = ""

   180→            slug = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '_', param_lines[0].strip().lower()).strip('_')[:40]

   184→                "parm": header_parts[-1].strip() if header_parts else "",

   186→                "after": after,

   189→            })
   190→            session["parameters"].append(slug)
   191→
   192→        sessions.append(session)
   193→
   194→    return {

   196→        "decisions": decisions,

   202→def evolve_to_charmeleon(md_path: str, usd_path: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   203→    """
   204→    Convert markdown memory to USD. Lossless.
   205→
   206→    1. Parse markdown
   207→    2. Create USD stage
   208→    3. Write typed prims
   209→    4. Archive original as memory_pre_evolution.md
   210→    5. Generate companion memory.md
   211→    """
   212→    try:
   213→        from pxr import Usd, Sdf
   214→    except ImportError:
   215→        return {"success": False, "error": "pxr not available"}
   216→
   217→    parsed = parse_markdown_memory(md_path)
   218→
   219→    stage = Usd.Stage.CreateNew(usd_path)
   220→    stage.DefinePrim("/SYNAPSE", "Xform")
   221→    stage.DefinePrim("/SYNAPSE/memory", "Xform")
   222→    stage.DefinePrim("/SYNAPSE/memory/sessions", "Xform")
   223→    stage.DefinePrim("/SYNAPSE/memory/decisions", "Xform")

   226→
   227→    # Write sessions

   229→        sid = session["id"]
   230→        prim = stage.DefinePrim(f"/SYNAPSE/memory/sessions/{sid}", "Xform")

   232→        prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:narrative", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(session["text"])
   233→
   234→    # Write decisions
   235→    for decision in parsed["decisions"]:
   236→        prim = stage.DefinePrim(f"/SYNAPSE/memory/decisions/{decision['slug']}", "Xform")
   237→        prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:choice", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(decision["choice"])

   239→        prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:date", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(decision["date"])
   240→
   241→    # Write parameters
   242→    for param in parsed["parameters"]:

   244→        prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:node", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(param["node"])
   245→        prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:parm", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(param["parm"])

   248→        prim.CreateAttribute("synapse:result", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set(param["result"])

   252→        "synapse:type": "scene_memory",

   254→    }
   255→    stage.GetRootLayer().Save()
   256→
   257→    # Archive original markdown
   258→    archive_path = md_path.replace(".md", "_pre_evolution.md")

   262→

   266→    return {

   268→        "sessions": len(parsed["sessions"]),
   269→        "decisions": len(parsed["decisions"]),
   270→        "parameters": len(parsed["parameters"]),

   275→def generate_companion_md(usd_path: str, md_path: str) -> None:
   276→    """Generate human-readable markdown from USD memory."""
   277→    try:
   278→        from pxr import Usd
   279→    except ImportError:
   280→        return
   281→
   282→    if not os.path.exists(usd_path):
   283→        return

   285→    stage = Usd.Stage.Open(usd_path)

   287→        "# Scene Memory (Charmeleon - auto-generated from USD)",

   291→        "---",
   292→        "",
   293→    ]

   295→    # Sessions
   296→    sessions_prim = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/SYNAPSE/memory/sessions")
   297→    if sessions_prim and sessions_prim.IsValid():

   300→            narrative_attr = session.GetAttribute("synapse:narrative")
   301→            date = date_attr.Get() if date_attr else session.GetName()
   302→            narrative = narrative_attr.Get() if narrative_attr else ""
   303→            lines.append(f"## Session {date}")
   304→            if narrative:
   305→                lines.append(narrative)
   306→            lines.append("")
   307→
   308→    # Decisions
   309→    decisions_prim = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/SYNAPSE/memory/decisions")
   310→    if decisions_prim and decisions_prim.IsValid():
   311→        children = list(decisions_prim.GetChildren())
   312→        if children:
   313→            lines.append("## Key Decisions")
   314→            lines.append("")
   315→            for d in sorted(children, key=lambda p: p.GetName()):
   316→                choice = d.GetAttribute("synapse:choice")
   317→                reasoning = d.GetAttribute("synapse:reasoning")
   318→                lines.append(f"### {d.GetName()}")
   319→                if choice:
   320→                    lines.append(f"**Choice:** {choice.Get()}")
   321→                if reasoning:
   322→                    lines.append(f"**Reasoning:** {reasoning.Get()}")
   323→                lines.append("")
   324→
   325→    with open(md_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   326→        f.write("\n".join(lines))
   327→
   328→
   329→def prune_memory(claude_dir: str, max_sessions_full: int = 5) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   330→    """
   331→    Compress old sessions to stay within token budget.
   332→
   333→    Never prunes: decisions, unresolved blockers, asset references.
   334→    """
   335→    md_path = os.path.join(claude_dir, "memory.md")
   336→    if not os.path.exists(md_path):
   337→        return {"pruned_sessions": 0, "new_size_kb": 0}
   338→
   339→    parsed = parse_markdown_memory(md_path)
   340→    sessions = parsed["sessions"]
   341→
   342→    if len(sessions) <= max_sessions_full:
   343→        return {"pruned_sessions": 0, "new_size_kb": round(os.path.getsize(md_path) / 1024, 2)}
   344→
   345→    # Keep recent sessions full, condense older ones
   346→    recent = sessions[-max_sessions_full:]
   347→    old = sessions[:-max_sessions_full]
   348→
   349→    pruned_count = len(old)
   350→
   351→    # Rebuild markdown with condensed old sessions
   352→    with open(md_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   353→        header_lines = []
   354→        for line in f:
   355→            if line.startswith("## Session"):
   356→                break
   357→            header_lines.append(line)
   358→
   359→    with open(md_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   360→        f.write("".join(header_lines))
   361→        f.write("\n## Archived Sessions (condensed)\n")
   362→        for session in old:
   363→            f.write(f"- {session['date']}: {len(session['text'].split(chr(10)))} lines")
   364→            if session["decisions"]:
   365→                f.write(f" | Decisions: {', '.join(session['decisions'])}")
   366→            f.write("\n")
   367→        f.write("\n")
   368→        for session in recent:
   369→            f.write(f"## Session {session['date']}\n{session['text']}\n\n")
   370→
   371→    new_size = round(os.path.getsize(md_path) / 1024, 2)
   372→    return {"pruned_sessions": pruned_count, "new_size_kb": new_size}
   373→
   374→
   375→def evolve_to_charizard(scene_usd_path: str, project_usd_path: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   376→    """
   377→    Set up composition arcs so scene memory sublayers project memory.
   378→    Scene-level opinions are stronger (override project defaults).
   379→    """
   380→    try:
   381→        from pxr import Usd, Sdf
   382→    except ImportError:
   383→        return {"success": False, "error": "pxr not available"}
   384→
   385→    if not os.path.exists(scene_usd_path) or not os.path.exists(project_usd_path):
   386→        return {"success": False, "error": "Missing USD files"}
   387→
   388→    stage = Usd.Stage.Open(scene_usd_path)
   389→    layer = stage.GetRootLayer()
   390→
   391→    # Add project.usd as sublayer (weaker -- scene opinions override)
   392→    project_rel = os.path.relpath(project_usd_path, os.path.dirname(scene_usd_path))
   393→    # Normalize to forward slashes for USD
   394→    project_rel = project_rel.replace("\\", "/")
   395→
   396→    existing = list(layer.subLayerPaths)
   397→    if project_rel not in existing:
   398→        existing.append(project_rel)
   399→        layer.subLayerPaths = existing
   400→
   401→    # Update evolution metadata
   402→    data = dict(layer.customLayerData)
   403→    data["synapse:evolution"] = "charizard"
   404→    layer.customLayerData = data
   405→
   406→    layer.Save()
   407→
   408→    return {"success": True, "sublayer": project_rel}

   160→
   161→            definition = hda_node.type().definition()

   237→
   238→            return {

   609→    def _handle_hda_list(self, payload: Dict) -> Dict:
   610→        """List all Synapse-authored HDAs currently loaded in Houdini.
   611→
   612→        Scans hou.hda.loadedFiles() and filters for HDAs with
   613→        'author=synapse' in their extraInfo. Read-only, no scene mutation.
   614→
   615→        Payload:
   616→            (no required parameters)
   617→        """

   619→            raise RuntimeError(_HOUDINI_UNAVAILABLE)

   621→        from .main_thread import run_on_main
   622→
   623→        def _on_main():
   624→            results = []
   625→            for hda_file in hou.hda.loadedFiles():
   626→                try:
   627→                    definitions = hou.hda.definitionsInFile(hda_file)
   628→                except Exception:
   629→                    continue
   630→                for defn in definitions:
   631→                    extra = ""
   632→                    try:
   633→                        extra = defn.extraInfo() or ""
   634→                    except Exception:
   635→                        continue
   636→                    if "author=synapse" not in extra:
   637→                        continue
   638→                    # Parse metadata from extraInfo
   639→                    meta = {}
   640→                    for part in extra.split(";"):
   641→                        if "=" in part:
   642→                            k, v = part.split("=", 1)
   643→                            meta[k.strip()] = v.strip()

   646→                        "label": defn.description(),

   650→                        "file_path": hda_file,

   A detailed system prompt addendum that teaches Claude how to design HDAs.
   This gets appended to the system prompt when the user types /hda.

   a) HDA design principles:
      - Clean parameter interface — only expose what artists need
      - Sensible defaults on every parameter
      - Internal nodes should be standard Houdini nodes (not execute_python)
      - Naming: operator_name is lowercase_underscore, label is Title Case
      - Version starts at 1.0.0
      - Save path defaults to $HIP/hda/ or $HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/hda/

      - "Sop" — geometry operations (most common)
      - "Lop" — USD/Solaris scene composition
      - "Object" — object-level containers
      - "Driver" — render/output operators
      - "Top" — PDG/TOPS task operators

      - Scatter points: grid → scatter → copytopoints
      - Deform: input → mountain → smooth → output
      - Fracture: input → voronoifracture → assemble → output
      - UV layout: input → uvflatten → uvlayout → output

   d) Common LOP HDA recipes:
      - Light rig: env_light + distant_light + dome_light → merge
      - Material setup: materiallibrary → assignmaterial
      - Render setup: karma_rop with standard settings

   e) Parameter promotion rules:
      - Always promote the "primary control" of each internal node
      - Group related parameters with folders
      - Use descriptive labels (not internal names)
      - Include min/max ranges where appropriate

   f) The hda_package tool schema reference (so Claude knows the exact format):
      - nodes: [{type, name, parms}, ...]
      - connections: [[src_name, dst_name, dst_input_idx], ...]
      - promoted_parms: [{node, parm, label}, ...]
      - Use "__input0" as src_name for subnet input connection

2. Function parse_hda_command(text: str) -> dict
   Parse the /hda command input.
   "/hda scatter points on a grid with density control" →
   {
       "description": "scatter points on a grid with density control",
       "raw": "/hda scatter points on a grid with density control"
   }

3. Function build_hda_messages(description: str, context: dict) -> list:
   Build the initial messages list for the HDA design conversation.
   The user message should be structured to guide Claude:
   "Design and build an HDA: {description}
    Current network: {context[network]}
    Use the hda_package tool to create it. Save to $HIP/hda/ if no path specified."

   Returns a default save path for the HDA.
   Uses $HIP/hda/{name}.hda if HIP is available, otherwise
   $HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/hda/{name}.hda.
   Creates the directory if it doesn't exist.
   hou import is optional (try/except).

5. Constant HDA_RECIPES -> dict
   A lookup of common HDA patterns keyed by keywords.
   Used for fast-path matching — if the user says "scatter",
   Claude can use the scatter recipe as a starting point.
   Format:
   {
       "scatter": {
           "category": "Sop",
           "nodes": [...],
           "connections": [...],
           "promoted_parms": [...]
       },
       ...
   }
   Include at least 6 recipes: scatter, fracture, deform, uv_layout,
   light_rig, material_setup.

- Read python/synapse/mcp/_tool_registry.py search for "hda_package" to see the tool schema
- Read python/synapse/server/handlers_hda.py to see _handle_hda_package implementation

      - Clean parameter interface — only expose what artists need
      - Sensible defaults on every parameter

data.prompt:
I need you to create a Prompt-to-HDA workflow module for the SYNAPSE panel.

CONTEXT:
- Repo root: C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE
- SYNAPSE already has an hda_package tool that creates HDAs from a description:
  Tool name: houdini_hda_package
  It takes: description, name, category, save_path, nodes (internal network),
  connections, promoted_parms, inputs
  See: python/synapse/mcp/_tool_registry.py (search for "hda_package")
  Handler: python/synapse/server/handlers_hda.py (_handle_hda_package)

- The panel will have a /hda command that:
  1. Takes a natural language description from the user
  2. Asks Claude to design the HDA (node types, connections, parameters)
  3. Claude calls hda_package tool with the complete specification
  4. Returns the packaged .hda file path

- The existing tool chain can already create the HDA. What's missing is the
  ORCHESTRATION layer that helps Claude design a GOOD HDA from a prompt:
  - Choosing the right internal nodes for the task
  - Setting up proper parameter interfaces (promoted parms)
  - Connecting nodes correctly
  - Setting sensible defaults
  - Picking the right category (Sop/Lop/Object/Driver/Top)

YOUR TASK:
Create python/synapse/panel/prompt_to_hda.py

This module provides:
1. HDA design guidance injected into the system prompt when /hda is active
2. A structured workflow that the panel orchestrates

REQUIREMENTS:

1. Constant HDA_DESIGN_PROMPT -> str
   A detailed system prompt addendum that teaches Claude how to design HDAs.
   This gets appended to the system prompt when the user types /hda.

   It should include:
   a) HDA design principles:
      - Clean parameter interface — only expose what artists need
      - Sensible defaults on every parameter
      - Internal nodes should be standard Houdini nodes (not execute_python)
      - Naming: operator_name is lowercase_underscore, label is Title Case
      - Version starts at 1.0.0
      - Save path defaults to $HIP/hda/ or $HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/hda/

   b) Category selection guide:
      - "Sop" — geometry operations (most common)
      - "Lop" — USD/Solaris scene composition
      - "Object" — object-level containers
      - "Driver" — render/output operators
      - "Top" — PDG/TOPS task operators

   c) Common SOP HDA recipes (node chains for frequent requests):
      - Scatter points: grid → scatter → copytopoints
      - Deform: input → mountain → smooth → output
      - Fracture: input → voronoifracture → assemble → output
      - UV layout: input → uvflatten → uvlayout → output

   d) Common LOP HDA recipes:
      - Light rig: env_light + distant_light + dome_light → merge
      - Material setup: materiallibrary → assignmaterial
      - Render setup: karma_rop with standard settings

   e) Parameter promotion rules:
      - Always promote the "primary control" of each internal node
      - Group related parameters with folders
      - Use descriptive labels (not internal names)
      - Include min/max ranges where appropriate

   f) The hda_package tool schema reference (so Claude knows the exact format):
      - nodes: [{type, name, parms}, ...]
      - connections: [[src_name, dst_name, dst_input_idx], ...]
      - promoted_parms: [{node, parm, label}, ...]
      - Use "__input0" as src_name for subnet input connection

2. Function parse_hda_command(text: str) -> dict
   Parse the /hda command input.
   "/hda scatter points on a grid with density control" →
   {
       "description": "scatter points on a grid with density control",
       "raw": "/hda scatter points on a grid with density control"
   }

3. Function build_hda_messages(description: str, context: dict) -> list:
   Build the initial messages list for the HDA design conversation.
   The user message should be structured to guide Claude:
   "Design and build an HDA: {description}
    Current network: {context[network]}
    Use the hda_package tool to create it. Save to $HIP/hda/ if no path specified."

4. Function default_save_path(name: str) -> str
   Returns a default save path for the HDA.
   Uses $HIP/hda/{name}.hda if HIP is available, otherwise
   $HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/hda/{name}.hda.
   Creates the directory if it doesn't exist.
   hou import is optional (try/except).

5. Constant HDA_RECIPES -> dict
   A lookup of common HDA patterns keyed by keywords.
   Used for fast-path matching — if the user says "scatter",
   Claude can use the scatter recipe as a starting point.
   Format:
   {
       "scatter": {
           "category": "Sop",
           "nodes": [...],
           "connections": [...],
           "promoted_parms": [...]
       },
       ...
   }
   Include at least 6 recipes: scatter, fracture, deform, uv_layout,
   light_rig, material_setup.

VERIFY:
- Read python/synapse/mcp/_tool_registry.py search for "hda_package" to see the tool schema
- Read python/synapse/server/handlers_hda.py to see _handle_hda_package implementation
- Run: python -c "from synapse.panel.prompt_to_hda import HDA_DESIGN_PROMPT, parse_hda_command; print(parse_hda_command('/hda scatter points')); print(len(HDA_DESIGN_PROMPT))"

DO NOT modify any existing files. Only create python/synapse/panel/prompt_to_hda.py

"""
Synapse Shot Login -- Context Hydration from Memory Layers

When an artist opens a hip file, this module loads context from all
available memory layers (project + scene), like logging into a shot
in a VFX pipeline.

Memory layers:
  Layer 1: Cognitive Substrate (global behavior -- system prompt, not files)
  Layer 2: Project Memory at $JOB/claude/project.md (or project.usd if evolved)
  Layer 3: Scene Memory at $HIP/claude/memory.md (or memory.usd if evolved)

Evolution stages: "flat" (markdown), "structured" (USD), "composed" (USD + arcs).
"""

import logging
import os
import time
from typing import Dict, Optional

logger = logging.getLogger("synapse.shot_login")

# Houdini API -- optional for testing outside Houdini
_HOU_AVAILABLE = False
try:
    import hou
    _HOU_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    hou = None

# Memory system -- optional, degrades gracefully
_MEMORY_AVAILABLE = False
try:
    from synapse.memory.scene_memory import (
        load_memory,
        get_evolution_stage,
        ensure_scene_structure,
        SCHEMA_VERSION,
    )
    _MEMORY_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    load_memory = None
    get_evolution_stage = None
    ensure_scene_structure = None
    SCHEMA_VERSION = "0.1.0"


# Map internal evolution names to the canonical stage names
_EVOLUTION_MAP = {
    "charmander": "flat",
    "charmeleon": "structured",
    "charizard": "composed",
    "flat": "flat",
    "structured": "structured",
    "composed": "composed",
    "none": "none",
}


def _normalize_evolution(stage: str) -> str:
    """Map internal evolution names to canonical flat/structured/composed."""
    return _EVOLUTION_MAP.get(stage, stage)


def shot_login(hip_path: str = "") -> dict:
    """
    Main entry point for shot login. Loads context from all memory layers.

    Args:
        hip_path: Path to the hip file. If empty, attempts hou.hipFile.path().

    Returns:
        Context dict with project/scene memory content, evolution stages,
        and a logged_in flag. Returns logged_in=False if memory system
        is unavailable.
    """
    # Resolve hip path
    if not hip_path:
        hip_path = _get_hip_path()

    if not hip_path:
        logger.warning("No hip path available -- returning minimal login")
        return _minimal_login("No hip path available")

    hip_path = os.path.normpath(hip_path)
    scene_dir = os.path.dirname(hip_path) if os.path.isfile(hip_path) else hip_path

    # Resolve project directory
    project_dir = _resolve_project_dir(scene_dir)

    # Paths to claude/ directories
    claude_scene = os.path.join(scene_dir, "claude")
    claude_project = os.path.join(project_dir, "claude") if project_dir else ""

    # Initialize directories and seed files
    ensure_claude_dir(scene_dir)
    if project_dir:
        ensure_claude_dir(project_dir)

    # Initialize scene memory if missing
    hip_name = os.path.basename(hip_path)
    init_scene_memory(claude_scene, hip_name)

    # Initialize project memory if missing
    if claude_project:
        _init_project_memory(claude_project, project_dir)

    # Load memory content
    project_context = ""
    project_evolution = "none"
    scene_context = ""
    scene_evolution = "none"

    if _MEMORY_AVAILABLE:
        # Load project memory
        if claude_project and os.path.isdir(claude_project):
            proj_data = load_memory(claude_project, "project")
            project_context = proj_data.get("content", "")
            project_evolution = _normalize_evolution(proj_data.get("evolution", "none"))

        # Load scene memory
        if os.path.isdir(claude_scene):
            scene_data = load_memory(claude_scene, "memory")
            scene_context = scene_data.get("content", "")
            scene_evolution = _normalize_evolution(scene_data.get("evolution", "none"))
    else:
        # Fallback: read files directly if memory module unavailable
        project_context, project_evolution = _load_memory_fallback(
            claude_project, "project"
        )
        scene_context, scene_evolution = _load_memory_fallback(
            claude_scene, "memory"
        )

    result = {
        "project_dir": project_dir or "",
        "scene_dir": scene_dir,
        "project_context": project_context,
        "scene_context": scene_context,
        "project_evolution": project_evolution,
        "scene_evolution": scene_evolution,
        "hip_file": hip_path,
        "logged_in": True,
    }

    logger.info(
        "Shot login complete: project=%s scene=%s",
        project_evolution,
        scene_evolution,
    )
    return result


def check_login_needed(current_hip: str, last_hip: str) -> bool:
    """
    Check if the hip file changed and we need to re-login.

    Args:
        current_hip: Current hip file path.
        last_hip: Previously logged-in hip file path.

    Returns:
        True if a new login is needed.
    """
    if not current_hip or not last_hip:
        return True
    return os.path.normpath(current_hip) != os.path.normpath(last_hip)


def format_memory_for_prompt(login_data: dict) -> str:
    """
    Convert login data into a formatted string for the system prompt.

    Includes project context, scene context, and a brief status line.
    Returns empty string if not logged in.
    """
    if not login_data.get("logged_in"):
        return ""

    parts = []

    # Status line
    proj_evo = login_data.get("project_evolution", "none")
    scene_evo = login_data.get("scene_evolution", "none")
    parts.append(f"Memory: project={proj_evo}, scene={scene_evo}")
    parts.append("")

    # Project context
    project_context = login_data.get("project_context", "")
    if project_context:
        parts.append("## Project Memory")
        parts.append("")
        parts.append(project_context.strip())
        parts.append("")

    # Scene context
    scene_context = login_data.get("scene_context", "")
    if scene_context:
        parts.append("## Scene Memory")
        parts.append("")
        parts.append(scene_context.strip())
        parts.append("")

    if not project_context and not scene_context:
        parts.append("No memory loaded for this shot.")

    return "\n".join(parts)


def ensure_claude_dir(base_dir: str) -> str:
    """
    Idempotently create {base_dir}/claude/ directory.

    Args:
        base_dir: Parent directory (scene dir or project dir).

    Returns:
        Path to the claude/ directory.
    """
    claude_dir = os.path.join(os.path.normpath(base_dir), "claude")
    os.makedirs(claude_dir, exist_ok=True)
    return claude_dir


def init_scene_memory(claude_dir: str, hip_name: str) -> None:
    """
    Create initial memory.md with header if it doesn't exist.

    Idempotent: never overwrites existing files.

    Args:
        claude_dir: Path to the claude/ directory.
        hip_name: Name of the hip file (for the header).
    """
    claude_dir = os.path.normpath(claude_dir)
    md_path = os.path.join(claude_dir, "memory.md")

    if os.path.exists(md_path):
        return

    # Ensure directory exists
    os.makedirs(claude_dir, exist_ok=True)

    now = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())
    content = (
        f"# Scene Memory: {hip_name}\n"
        f"# Created: {now}\n"
        f"# Evolution: flat\n"
        f"# Schema: {SCHEMA_VERSION}\n"
        "\n---\n\n"
    )

    with open(md_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(content)

    logger.info("Initialized scene memory: %s", md_path)


# =============================================================================
# INTERNAL HELPERS
# =============================================================================


def _get_hip_path() -> str:
    """Get current hip file path from Houdini, or empty string."""
    if not _HOU_AVAILABLE:
        return ""
    try:
        path = hou.hipFile.path()
        # hou.hipFile.path() returns "untitled.hip" for unsaved files
        if path and os.path.basename(path) != "untitled.hip":
            return path
        return ""
    except Exception:
        return ""


def _resolve_project_dir(scene_dir: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Resolve the project directory.

    Priority:
      1. $JOB environment variable (via hou or os.environ)
      2. Walk up from scene_dir looking for a directory with a claude/ folder
    """
    # Try $JOB from Houdini
    job_dir = None
    if _HOU_AVAILABLE:
        try:
            job_dir = hou.getenv("JOB")
        except Exception:
            pass

    # Try $JOB from environment
    if not job_dir:
        job_dir = os.environ.get("JOB", "")

    if job_dir and os.path.isdir(job_dir):
        return os.path.normpath(job_dir)

    # Walk up from scene_dir looking for claude/ folder
    current = os.path.normpath(scene_dir)
    for _ in range(10):  # max depth to avoid infinite loops
        parent = os.path.dirname(current)
        if parent == current:
            break  # filesystem root
        candidate_claude = os.path.join(parent, "claude")
        if os.path.isdir(candidate_claude):
            return parent
        current = parent

    # No project dir found -- use scene_dir as fallback
    return None


def _init_project_memory(claude_dir: str, project_dir: str) -> None:
    """Create initial project.md with header if it doesn't exist."""
    claude_dir = os.path.normpath(claude_dir)
    md_path = os.path.join(claude_dir, "project.md")

    if os.path.exists(md_path):
        return

    os.makedirs(claude_dir, exist_ok=True)

    project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(project_dir))
    now = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())
    content = (
        f"# Project Memory: {project_name}\n"
        f"# Created: {now}\n"
        f"# Evolution: flat\n"
        f"# Schema: {SCHEMA_VERSION}\n"
        "\n---\n\n"
        "## Pipeline Configuration\n\n"
        "## Key Decisions\n\n"
        "## Notes\n"
    )

    with open(md_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(content)

    logger.info("Initialized project memory: %s", md_path)


def _load_memory_fallback(
    claude_dir: str, name: str
) -> tuple:
    """
    Fallback memory loader when synapse.memory is not available.

    Returns (content, evolution_stage) tuple.
    """
    if not claude_dir or not os.path.isdir(claude_dir):
        return "", "none"

    usd_path = os.path.join(claude_dir, f"{name}.usd")
    md_path = os.path.join(claude_dir, f"{name}.md")

    # Prefer USD if it exists and isn't an agent stub
    if os.path.exists(usd_path):
        try:
            with open(usd_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                content = f.read()
            if '"synapse:type" = "agent_state"' not in content:
                # Check for composition arcs
                if "subLayers" in content or "references" in content:
                    return content, "composed"
                return content, "structured"
        except Exception:
            pass

    # Fall back to markdown
    if os.path.exists(md_path):
        try:
            with open(md_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                content = f.read()
            return content, "flat"
        except Exception:
            return "", "none"

    return "", "none"


def _minimal_login(reason: str = "") -> dict:
    """Return a minimal login dict when full login isn't possible."""
    return {
        "project_dir": "",
        "scene_dir": "",
        "project_context": "",
        "scene_context": "",
        "project_evolution": "none",
        "scene_evolution": "none",
        "hip_file": "",
        "logged_in": False,
        "reason": reason,
    }

HDA_DESIGN_PROMPT = """\
## HDA Design Mode

You are now in HDA design mode. The artist wants you to design and build a
Houdini Digital Asset (HDA) from their description. Follow these principles
and use the `hda_package` tool to create the HDA.

### Design Principles

1. **Clean parameter interface** -- only expose what the artist needs to control.
   Internal plumbing stays hidden. Every promoted parameter should have a
   descriptive label, not the raw internal name.
2. **Sensible defaults** -- every parameter must have a reasonable default value
   so the HDA works out of the box without any tweaking.
3. **Standard nodes only** -- build the internal network from standard Houdini
   nodes (SOPs, LOPs, etc.). Do NOT use `execute_python` or `attribwrangle`
   with complex VEX unless explicitly requested. Keep it maintainable.
4. **Naming conventions**:
   - `operator_name`: lowercase_underscore (e.g. `scatter_on_surface`)
   - `operator_label`: Title Case (e.g. `Scatter On Surface`)
   - Node names inside: descriptive lowercase (e.g. `scatter1`, `grid_base`)
5. **Version**: always start at `1.0.0`.
6. **Save path**: default to `$HIP/hda/<name>.hda`. If no `$HIP` is set,
   use `$HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/hda/<name>.hda`.
7. **Finish with a null node named OUT** -- set display/render flags on it.
   This is standard Houdini practice for clean subnet outputs.
8. **Inputs**: use `__input0` as the source name for the first subnet input,
   `__input1` for the second, etc. Only add inputs when the HDA needs
   upstream geometry.

### Category Selection Guide

Choose the category based on what the HDA does:

| Category   | When to Use                                          | Examples                               |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| **Sop**    | Geometry operations (most common)                    | Scatter, fracture, deform, UV, meshing |
| **Lop**    | USD / Solaris scene composition                      | Light rigs, material setup, render     |
| **Object** | Object-level containers (rare for HDAs)              | Character rig, asset container         |
| **Driver** | Render / output operators                            | Custom render submit, export pipeline  |
| **Top**    | PDG / TOPS task graph operators                      | Batch processing, wedging              |

Most artist requests will be **Sop** or **Lop**. Default to **Sop** if unclear.

### Common SOP Recipes

Use these as starting points when the request matches:

- **Scatter points on surface**: grid -> scatter -> copytopoints -> OUT
  Promote: grid size, point count, seed
- **Deform geometry**: input -> mountain -> smooth -> OUT
  Promote: amplitude, frequency, smooth iterations
- **Fracture**: input -> voronoifracture -> assemble -> OUT
  Promote: piece count, seed, pack option
- **UV layout**: input -> uvflatten -> uvlayout -> OUT
  Promote: island padding
- **Remesh**: input -> remesh -> OUT
  Promote: target edge length
- **Boolean**: input0 + input1 -> boolean -> OUT
  Promote: operation type (union/intersect/subtract)

### Common LOP Recipes

- **Light rig**: key_light + fill_light + dome_light -> merge
  Promote: each light's exposure. Intensity always 1.0 (Lighting Law).
  Use `light::2.0` for directional, `domelight::2.0` for environment.
  Exposure controls brightness -- NEVER set intensity above 1.0.
- **Material setup**: materiallibrary -> assignmaterial -> OUT
  Promote: material paths, geometry assignments
- **Render setup**: karmarenderproperties -> OUT
  Promote: pixel samples, convergence mode

### Parameter Promotion Rules

1. **Promote the primary control** of each internal node -- the parameter
   the artist is most likely to adjust.
2. **Group related parameters** by using descriptive labels that form a
   logical reading order.
3. **Use descriptive labels**: "Point Count" not "npts", "Noise Amplitude"
   not "height", "Random Seed" not "seed".
4. **Include min/max context** in the label when helpful:
   "Smooth Iterations (1-100)" for iteration counts.

### hda_package Tool Schema

Call the `hda_package` tool with this structure:

```json
{
  "description": "What the HDA does (free text)",
  "name": "operator_name_lowercase",
  "category": "Sop",
  "save_path": "$HIP/hda/operator_name.hda",
  "inputs": ["Input geometry description"],
  "nodes": [
    {"type": "node_type", "name": "node_name", "parms": {"parm": value}},
    {"type": "null", "name": "OUT", "parms": {}}
  ],
  "connections": [
    ["__input0", "first_node", "0"],
    ["first_node", "second_node", "0"],
    ["second_node", "OUT", "0"]
  ],
  "promoted_parms": [
    {"node": "node_name", "parm": "parm_name", "label": "Artist-Friendly Label"}
  ]
}
```

**Connection format**: `[source_name, destination_name, destination_input_index]`
- Use `"__input0"` for the first subnet input, `"__input1"` for the second
- `destination_input_index` is a string (e.g. `"0"`, `"1"`)

### Workflow

1. Analyze the artist's description
2. Choose the right category (Sop/Lop/Object/Driver/Top)
3. Design the internal node network (types, names, default parm values)
4. Decide which parameters to promote (artist-facing controls)
5. Set up connections (linear chain or branching as needed)
6. Call `hda_package` with the complete specification
7. Report the result: HDA path, operator type, promoted parameters
"""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Command parser
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_HDA_CMD_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"^/hda\s+(.+)$",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL,
)


def parse_hda_command(text: str) -> dict:
    """Parse a ``/hda`` command string into a structured dict.

    Parameters
    ----------
    text : str
        The raw command text, e.g. ``"/hda scatter points on a grid"``.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``{"description": str, "raw": str}`` on success,
        ``{"description": "", "raw": str}`` if no description was provided.
    """
    text = text.strip()
    match = _HDA_CMD_PATTERN.match(text)
    if match:
        description = match.group(1).strip()
    else:
        description = ""
    return {
        "description": description,
        "raw": text,
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Message builder
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_hda_messages(description: str, context: dict | None = None) -> list:
    """Build the initial message list for the HDA design conversation.

    Parameters
    ----------
    description : str
        The artist's natural language description of the desired HDA.
    context : dict, optional
        Scene context dict. Recognized keys:

        - ``network`` (str): Current network path (e.g. ``"/obj/geo1"``)
        - ``selected_nodes`` (list[str]): Currently selected node paths
        - ``hip_path`` (str): Current HIP file path

    Returns
    -------
    list[dict]
        A list of message dicts suitable for the Anthropic API.
    """
    if context is None:
        context = {}

    network = context.get("network", "/obj")
    selected = context.get("selected_nodes", [])
    hip_path = context.get("hip_path", "")

    parts = [f"Design and build an HDA: {description}"]

    if network:
        parts.append(f"Current network context: {network}")

    if selected:
        parts.append(f"Selected nodes: {', '.join(selected)}")

    if hip_path:
        parts.append(f"HIP file: {hip_path}")

    parts.append(
        "Use the hda_package tool to create it. "
        "Save to $HIP/hda/ if no path specified."
    )

    user_content = "\n".join(parts)

    return [
        {"role": "user", "content": user_content},
    ]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Default save path
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def default_save_path(name: str) -> str:
    """Return a default save path for an HDA file.

    Tries ``$HIP/hda/<name>.hda`` first (requires ``hou`` module).
    Falls back to ``$HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/hda/<name>.hda``.
    Creates the parent directory if it does not exist.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        The operator name (e.g. ``"scatter_on_surface"``).

    Returns
    -------
    str
        Absolute path to the .hda file.
    """
    hda_dir = None

    # Try $HIP/hda/ via hou module
    try:
        import hou
        hip = hou.getenv("HIP")
        if hip:
            hda_dir = os.path.join(hip, "hda")
    except ImportError:
        pass

    # Fallback: $HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/hda/
    if hda_dir is None:
        pref_dir = os.environ.get("HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR", "")
        if not pref_dir:
            # Best-effort default
            pref_dir = os.path.expanduser("~/houdini21.0")
        hda_dir = os.path.join(pref_dir, "hda")

    # Ensure directory exists
    os.makedirs(hda_dir, exist_ok=True)

    return os.path.join(hda_dir, f"{name}.hda")

data.prompt:
I need you to create a Prompt-to-HDA workflow module for the SYNAPSE panel.

CONTEXT:
- Repo root: C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE
- SYNAPSE already has an hda_package tool that creates HDAs from a description:
  Tool name: houdini_hda_package
  It takes: description, name, category, save_path, nodes (internal network),
  connections, promoted_parms, inputs
  See: python/synapse/mcp/_tool_registry.py (search for "hda_package")
  Handler: python/synapse/server/handlers_hda.py (_handle_hda_package)

- The panel will have a /hda command that:
  1. Takes a natural language description from the user
  2. Asks Claude to design the HDA (node types, connections, parameters)
  3. Claude calls hda_package tool with the complete specification
  4. Returns the packaged .hda file path

- The existing tool chain can already create the HDA. What's missing is the
  ORCHESTRATION layer that helps Claude design a GOOD HDA from a prompt:
  - Choosing the right internal nodes for the task
  - Setting up proper parameter interfaces (promoted parms)
  - Connecting nodes correctly
  - Setting sensible defaults
  - Picking the right category (Sop/Lop/Object/Driver/Top)

YOUR TASK:
Create python/synapse/panel/prompt_to_hda.py

This module provides:
1. HDA design guidance injected into the system prompt when /hda is active
2. A structured workflow that the panel orchestrates

REQUIREMENTS:

1. Constant HDA_DESIGN_PROMPT -> str
   A detailed system prompt addendum that teaches Claude how to design HDAs.
   This gets appended to the system prompt when the user types /hda.

   It should include:
   a) HDA design principles:
      - Clean parameter interface — only expose what artists need
      - Sensible defaults on every parameter
      - Internal nodes should be standard Houdini nodes (not execute_python)
      - Naming: operator_name is lowercase_underscore, label is Title Case
      - Version starts at 1.0.0
      - Save path defaults to $HIP/hda/ or $HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/hda/

   b) Category selection guide:
      - "Sop" — geometry operations (most common)
      - "Lop" — USD/Solaris scene composition
      - "Object" — object-level containers
      - "Driver" — render/output operators
      - "Top" — PDG/TOPS task operators

   c) Common SOP HDA recipes (node chains for frequent requests):
      - Scatter points: grid → scatter → copytopoints
      - Deform: input → mountain → smooth → output
      - Fracture: input → voronoifracture → assemble → output
      - UV layout: input → uvflatten → uvlayout → output

   d) Common LOP HDA recipes:
      - Light rig: env_light + distant_light + dome_light → merge
      - Material setup: materiallibrary → assignmaterial
      - Render setup: karma_rop with standard settings

   e) Parameter promotion rules:
      - Always promote the "primary control" of each internal node
      - Group related parameters with folders
      - Use descriptive labels (not internal names)
      - Include min/max ranges where appropriate

   f) The hda_package tool schema reference (so Claude knows the exact format):
      - nodes: [{type, name, parms}, ...]
      - connections: [[src_name, dst_name, dst_input_idx], ...]
      - promoted_parms: [{node, parm, label}, ...]
      - Use "__input0" as src_name for subnet input connection

2. Function parse_hda_command(text: str) -> dict
   Parse the /hda command input.
   "/hda scatter points on a grid with density control" →
   {
       "description": "scatter points on a grid with density control",
       "raw": "/hda scatter points on a grid with density control"
   }

3. Function build_hda_messages(description: str, context: dict) -> list:
   Build the initial messages list for the HDA design conversation.
   The user message should be structured to guide Claude:
   "Design and build an HDA: {description}
    Current network: {context[network]}
    Use the hda_package tool to create it. Save to $HIP/hda/ if no path specified."

4. Function default_save_path(name: str) -> str
   Returns a default save path for the HDA.
   Uses $HIP/hda/{name}.hda if HIP is available, otherwise
   $HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/hda/{name}.hda.
   Creates the directory if it doesn't exist.
   hou import is optional (try/except).

5. Constant HDA_RECIPES -> dict
   A lookup of common HDA patterns keyed by keywords.
   Used for fast-path matching — if the user says "scatter",
   Claude can use the scatter recipe as a starting point.
   Format:
   {
       "scatter": {
           "category": "Sop",
           "nodes": [...],
           "connections": [...],
           "promoted_parms": [...]
       },
       ...
   }
   Include at least 6 recipes: scatter, fracture, deform, uv_layout,
   light_rig, material_setup.

VERIFY:
- Read python/synapse/mcp/_tool_registry.py search for "hda_package" to see the tool schema
- Read python/synapse/server/handlers_hda.py to see _handle_hda_package implementation
- Run: python -c "from synapse.panel.prompt_to_hda import HDA_DESIGN_PROMPT, parse_hda_command; print(parse_hda_command('/hda scatter points')); print(len(HDA_DESIGN_PROMPT))"

DO NOT modify any existing files. Only create python/synapse/panel/prompt_to_hda.py

  Tool name: houdini_hda_package

  connections, promoted_parms, inputs
  See: python/synapse/mcp/_tool_registry.py (search for "hda_package")
  Handler: python/synapse/server/handlers_hda.py (_handle_hda_package)

- The panel will have a /hda command that:
  1. Takes a natural language description from the user
  2. Asks Claude to design the HDA (node types, connections, parameters)
  3. Claude calls hda_package tool with the complete specification
  4. Returns the packaged .hda file path

- The existing tool chain can already create the HDA. What's missing is the
  ORCHESTRATION layer that helps Claude design a GOOD HDA from a prompt:
  - Choosing the right internal nodes for the task
  - Setting up proper parameter interfaces (promoted parms)
  - Connecting nodes correctly
  - Setting sensible defaults
  - Picking the right category (Sop/Lop/Object/Driver/Top)

YOUR TASK:
Create python/synapse/panel/prompt_to_hda.py

This module provides:
1. HDA design guidance injected into the system prompt when /hda is active
2. A structured workflow that the panel orchestrates

REQUIREMENTS:

1. Constant HDA_DESIGN_PROMPT -> str
   A detailed system prompt addendum that teaches Claude how to design HDAs.
   This gets appended to the system prompt when the user types /hda.

   It should include:
   a) HDA design principles:
      - Clean parameter interface — only expose what artists need
      - Sensible defaults on every parameter
      - Internal nodes should be standard Houdini nodes (not execute_python)
      - Naming: operator_name is lowercase_underscore, label is Title Case
      - Version starts at 1.0.0
      - Save path defaults to $HIP/hda/ or $HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/hda/

   b) Category selection guide:
      - "Sop" — geometry operations (most common)
      - "Lop" — USD/Solaris scene composition
      - "Object" — object-level containers
      - "Driver" — render/output operators
      - "Top" — PDG/TOPS task operators

   c) Common SOP HDA recipes (node chains for frequent requests):
      - Scatter points: grid → scatter → copytopoints
      - Deform: input → mountain → smooth → output
      - Fracture: input → voronoifracture → assemble → output
      - UV layout: input → uvflatten → uvlayout → output

   d) Common LOP HDA recipes:
      - Light rig: env_light + distant_light + dome_light → merge
      - Material setup: materiallibrary → assignmaterial
      - Render setup: karma_rop with standard settings

   e) Parameter promotion rules:
      - Always promote the "primary control" of each internal node
      - Group related parameters with folders
      - Use descriptive labels (not internal names)
      - Include min/max ranges where appropriate

   f) The hda_package tool schema reference (so Claude knows the exact format):
      - nodes: [{type, name, parms}, ...]
      - connections: [[src_name, dst_name, dst_input_idx], ...]
      - promoted_parms: [{node, parm, label}, ...]
      - Use "__input0" as src_name for subnet input connection

2. Function parse_hda_command(text: str) -> dict
   Parse the /hda command input.
   "/hda scatter points on a grid with density control" →
   {
       "description": "scatter points on a grid with density control",
       "raw": "/hda scatter points on a grid with density control"
   }

3. Function build_hda_messages(description: str, context: dict) -> list:
   Build the initial messages list for the HDA design conversation.
   The user message should be structured to guide Claude:
   "Design and build an HDA: {description}
    Current network: {context[network]}
    Use the hda_package tool to create it. Save to $HIP/hda/ if no path specified."

4. Function default_save_path(name: str) -> str
   Returns a default save path for the HDA.
   Uses $HIP/hda/{name}.hda if HIP is available, otherwise
   $HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/hda/{name}.hda.
   Creates the directory if it doesn't exist.
   hou import is optional (try/except).

5. Constant HDA_RECIPES -> dict
   A lookup of common HDA patterns keyed by keywords.
   Used for fast-path matching — if the user says "scatter",
   Claude can use the scatter recipe as a starting point.
   Format:
   {
       "scatter": {
           "category": "Sop",
           "nodes": [...],
           "connections": [...],
           "promoted_parms": [...]
       },
       ...
   }
   Include at least 6 recipes: scatter, fracture, deform, uv_layout,
   light_rig, material_setup.

VERIFY:
- Read python/synapse/mcp/_tool_registry.py search for "hda_package" to see the tool schema
- Read python/synapse/server/handlers_hda.py to see _handle_hda_package implementation
- Run: python -c "from synapse.panel.prompt_to_hda import HDA_DESIGN_PROMPT, parse_hda_command; print(parse_hda_command('/hda scatter points')); print(len(HDA_DESIGN_PROMPT))"

DO NOT modify any existing files. Only create python/synapse/panel/prompt_to_hda.py

   526→    def _on_copy_ws_path(self):
   527→        """Copy the WebSocket URL to clipboard."""
   528→        if self._copy_text(_WS_URL):
   529→            self._log_activity("Copied: {}".format(_WS_URL), "success")

   533→    @staticmethod
   534→    def _copy_text(text):
   535→        """Copy text to clipboard via clip.exe (Windows) or Qt fallback."""
   536→        import platform, subprocess
   537→        if platform.system() == "Windows":
   538→            try:
   539→                p = subprocess.run(
   540→                    ["clip"], input=text.encode("utf-8"),
   541→                    creationflags=0x08000000, timeout=5,
   542→                )
   543→                return p.returncode == 0
   544→            except Exception:
   545→                pass
   546→        try:
   547→            app = QtWidgets.QApplication.instance() or QtGui.QGuiApplication.instance()
   548→            if app:
   549→                app.clipboard().setText(text)
   550→                return True
   551→        except Exception:
   552→            pass
   553→        return False
