   557→    def _log_activity(self, message, level="info"):
   558→        """Add a timestamped entry to the activity log."""
   559→        timestamp = time.strftime("%H:%M:%S")
   560→
   561→        color_map = {
   562→            "info": SILVER if _HAS_DESIGN else "#999999",
   563→            "success": GROW if _HAS_DESIGN else "#00E676",
   564→            "warning": WARN if _HAS_DESIGN else "#FFAB00",
   565→            "error": ERROR if _HAS_DESIGN else "#FF3D71",
   566→            "action": SIGNAL if _HAS_DESIGN else "#00D4FF",
   567→        }
   568→        color = color_map.get(level, color_map["info"])
   569→
   570→        html = (
   571→            f'<span style="color: {SLATE if _HAS_DESIGN else "#555555"};">'
   572→            f'{timestamp}</span> '
   573→            f'<span style="color: {color};">{message}</span>'
   574→        )
   575→        self._log.append(html)
   576→
   577→        # Trim if too long
   578→        doc = self._log.document()
   579→        if doc.blockCount() > _ACTIVITY_MAX_LINES:
   580→            cursor = self._log.textCursor()
   581→            cursor.movePosition(QtGui.QTextCursor.Start)
   582→            cursor.movePosition(
   583→                QtGui.QTextCursor.Down,
   584→                QtGui.QTextCursor.KeepAnchor,
   585→                doc.blockCount() - _ACTIVITY_MAX_LINES,
   586→            )
   587→            cursor.removeSelectedText()

   720→    def _chat(self, user_text):
   721→        """Send a message to Claude and stream the response."""
   722→        # Display user message
   723→        user_color = SIGNAL if _HAS_DESIGN else "#00D4FF"
   724→        user_html = (
   725→            '<div style="margin: 8px 0 4px 0;">'
   726→            '<b style="color: {};">You</b></div>'
   727→            '<div style="margin: 0 0 8px 10px;">{}</div>'
   728→        ).format(user_color, user_text.replace("\n", "<br>"))
   729→        self._chat_display.append(user_html)
   730→
   731→        # Append to conversation history
   732→        self._messages.append({"role": "user", "content": user_text})
   733→
   734→        # Build system prompt
   735→        system_prompt = ""
   736→        try:
   737→            from synapse.panel.system_prompt import build_system_prompt
   738→            system_prompt = build_system_prompt(self._gather_context())
   739→        except ImportError:
   740→            system_prompt = (
   741→                "You are SYNAPSE, an AI co-pilot inside Houdini 21. "
   742→                "Help the artist with VFX tasks."
   743→            )
   744→
   745→        # Try importing the full ClaudeWorker with tool support
   746→        WorkerClass = _FallbackClaudeWorker
   747→        _has_tools = False
   748→        try:
   749→            from synapse.panel.claude_worker import ClaudeWorker
   750→            WorkerClass = ClaudeWorker
   751→            _has_tools = True
   752→        except ImportError:
   753→            self._sys("Tool-use worker not available -- using text-only mode.")
   754→
   755→        # Disable send while streaming
   756→        self._send_btn.setEnabled(False)
   757→        self._streaming_text = ""
   758→
   759→        # Prepare assistant message placeholder
   760→        synapse_color = GROW if _HAS_DESIGN else "#00E676"
   761→        self._chat_display.append(
   762→            '<div style="margin: 8px 0 4px 0;">'
   763→            '<b style="color: {};">SYNAPSE</b></div>'
   764→            '<div id="stream_target" style="margin: 0 0 8px 10px;">'.format(
   765→                synapse_color
   766→            )
   767→        )
   768→
   769→        # Create and wire worker
   770→        self._worker = WorkerClass(
   771→            messages=self._messages,
   772→            system_prompt=system_prompt,
   773→            parent=self,
   774→        )
   775→        self._worker.token_received.connect(self._on_token)
   776→        self._worker.stream_done.connect(self._on_done)
   777→        self._worker.stream_error.connect(self._on_error)
   778→
   779→        # Wire tool signals if the full worker is in use
   780→        if _has_tools:
   781→            executor = self._ensure_tool_executor()
   782→            if executor is not None:
   783→                self._worker.tool_requested.connect(executor.execute_tool)
   784→            self._worker.tool_status.connect(self._on_tool_status)
   785→
   786→        self._worker.start()
   787→
   788→    def _on_token(self, text):
   789→        """Handle a streamed text token from the worker."""
   790→        self._streaming_text += text
   791→        # Move cursor to end and insert text
   792→        cursor = self._chat_display.textCursor()
   793→        cursor.movePosition(QtGui.QTextCursor.End)
   794→        cursor.insertText(text)
   795→        self._chat_display.setTextCursor(cursor)
   796→        sb = self._chat_display.verticalScrollBar()
   797→        sb.setValue(sb.maximum())
   798→
   799→    def _on_done(self):
   800→        """Handle stream completion."""
   801→        # Close the streaming div
   802→        cursor = self._chat_display.textCursor()
   803→        cursor.movePosition(QtGui.QTextCursor.End)
   804→        cursor.insertHtml("</div>")
   805→        self._chat_display.setTextCursor(cursor)
   806→
   807→        self._send_btn.setEnabled(True)
   808→
   809→        # Sync conversation history from the worker (includes tool loop turns)
   810→        if self._worker:
   811→            self._messages = self._worker.get_messages()

   158→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   159→# HDA Design Prompt -- injected into system prompt when /hda is active
   160→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   161→
   162→HDA_DESIGN_PROMPT = """\
   163→## HDA Design Mode
   164→
   165→You are now in HDA design mode. The artist wants you to design and build a
   166→Houdini Digital Asset (HDA) from their description. Follow these principles
   167→and use the `hda_package` tool to create the HDA.
   168→
   169→### Design Principles
   170→
   171→1. **Clean parameter interface** -- only expose what the artist needs to control.
   172→   Internal plumbing stays hidden. Every promoted parameter should have a
   173→   descriptive label, not the raw internal name.
   174→2. **Sensible defaults** -- every parameter must have a reasonable default value
   175→   so the HDA works out of the box without any tweaking.
   176→3. **Standard nodes only** -- build the internal network from standard Houdini
   177→   nodes (SOPs, LOPs, etc.). Do NOT use `execute_python` or `attribwrangle`
   178→   with complex VEX unless explicitly requested. Keep it maintainable.
   179→4. **Naming conventions**:
   180→   - `operator_name`: lowercase_underscore (e.g. `scatter_on_surface`)
   181→   - `operator_label`: Title Case (e.g. `Scatter On Surface`)
   182→   - Node names inside: descriptive lowercase (e.g. `scatter1`, `grid_base`)
   183→5. **Version**: always start at `1.0.0`.
   184→6. **Save path**: default to `$HIP/hda/<name>.hda`. If no `$HIP` is set,
   185→   use `$HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/hda/<name>.hda`.
   186→7. **Finish with a null node named OUT** -- set display/render flags on it.
   187→   This is standard Houdini practice for clean subnet outputs.
   188→8. **Inputs**: use `__input0` as the source name for the first subnet input,
   189→   `__input1` for the second, etc. Only add inputs when the HDA needs
   190→   upstream geometry.
   191→
   192→### Category Selection Guide
   193→
   194→Choose the category based on what the HDA does:
   195→
   196→| Category   | When to Use                                          | Examples                               |
   197→|------------|------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
   198→| **Sop**    | Geometry operations (most common)                    | Scatter, fracture, deform, UV, meshing |
   199→| **Lop**    | USD / Solaris scene composition                      | Light rigs, material setup, render     |
   200→| **Object** | Object-level containers (rare for HDAs)              | Character rig, asset container         |
   201→| **Driver** | Render / output operators                            | Custom render submit, export pipeline  |
   202→| **Top**    | PDG / TOPS task graph operators                      | Batch processing, wedging              |
   203→
   204→Most artist requests will be **Sop** or **Lop**. Default to **Sop** if unclear.
   205→
   206→### Common SOP Recipes
   207→
   208→Use these as starting points when the request matches:
   209→
   210→- **Scatter points on surface**: grid -> scatter -> copytopoints -> OUT
   211→  Promote: grid size, point count, seed
   212→- **Deform geometry**: input -> mountain -> smooth -> OUT
   213→  Promote: amplitude, frequency, smooth iterations
   214→- **Fracture**: input -> voronoifracture -> assemble -> OUT
   215→  Promote: piece count, seed, pack option
   216→- **UV layout**: input -> uvflatten -> uvlayout -> OUT
   217→  Promote: island padding
   218→- **Remesh**: input -> remesh -> OUT
   219→  Promote: target edge length
   220→- **Boolean**: input0 + input1 -> boolean -> OUT
   221→  Promote: operation type (union/intersect/subtract)
   222→
   223→### Common LOP Recipes
   224→
   225→- **Light rig**: key_light + fill_light + dome_light -> merge
   226→  Promote: each light's exposure. Intensity always 1.0 (Lighting Law).
   227→  Use `light::2.0` for directional, `domelight::2.0` for environment.
   228→  Exposure controls brightness -- NEVER set intensity above 1.0.
   229→- **Material setup**: materiallibrary -> assignmaterial -> OUT
   230→  Promote: material paths, geometry assignments
   231→- **Render setup**: karmarenderproperties -> OUT
   232→  Promote: pixel samples, convergence mode
   233→
   234→### Parameter Promotion Rules
   235→
   236→1. **Promote the primary control** of each internal node -- the parameter
   237→   the artist is most likely to adjust.
   238→2. **Group related parameters** by using descriptive labels that form a
   239→   logical reading order.
   240→3. **Use descriptive labels**: "Point Count" not "npts", "Noise Amplitude"
   241→   not "height", "Random Seed" not "seed".
   242→4. **Include min/max context** in the label when helpful:
   243→   "Smooth Iterations (1-100)" for iteration counts.
   244→
   245→### hda_package Tool Schema
   246→
   247→Call the `hda_package` tool with this structure:
   248→
   249→```json
   250→{
   251→  "description": "What the HDA does (free text)",
   252→  "name": "operator_name_lowercase",
   253→  "category": "Sop",
   254→  "save_path": "$HIP/hda/operator_name.hda",
   255→  "inputs": ["Input geometry description"],
   256→  "nodes": [
   257→    {"type": "node_type", "name": "node_name", "parms": {"parm": value}},
   258→    {"type": "null", "name": "OUT", "parms": {}}
   259→  ],
   260→  "connections": [
   261→    ["__input0", "first_node", "0"],
   262→    ["first_node", "second_node", "0"],
   263→    ["second_node", "OUT", "0"]
   264→  ],
   265→  "promoted_parms": [
   266→    {"node": "node_name", "parm": "parm_name", "label": "Artist-Friendly Label"}
   267→  ]
   268→}
   269→```
   270→
   271→**Connection format**: `[source_name, destination_name, destination_input_index]`
   272→- Use `"__input0"` for the first subnet input, `"__input1"` for the second
   273→- `destination_input_index` is a string (e.g. `"0"`, `"1"`)
   274→
   275→### Workflow
   276→
   277→1. Analyze the artist's description
   278→2. Choose the right category (Sop/Lop/Object/Driver/Top)
   279→3. Design the internal node network (types, names, default parm values)
   280→4. Decide which parameters to promote (artist-facing controls)
   281→5. Set up connections (linear chain or branching as needed)
   282→6. Call `hda_package` with the complete specification
   283→7. Report the result: HDA path, operator type, promoted parameters
   284→"""
   285→
   286→
   287→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   288→# Command parser
   289→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   290→
   291→_HDA_CMD_PATTERN = re.compile(
   292→    r"^/hda\s+(.+)$",
   293→    re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL,
   294→)
   295→
   296→
   297→def parse_hda_command(text: str) -> dict:
   298→    """Parse a ``/hda`` command string into a structured dict.
   299→
   300→    Parameters
   301→    ----------
   302→    text : str
   303→        The raw command text, e.g. ``"/hda scatter points on a grid"``.
   304→
   305→    Returns
   306→    -------
   307→    dict
   308→        ``{"description": str, "raw": str}`` on success,
   309→        ``{"description": "", "raw": str}`` if no description was provided.
   310→    """
   311→    text = text.strip()
   312→    match = _HDA_CMD_PATTERN.match(text)
   313→    if match:
   314→        description = match.group(1).strip()
   315→    else:
   316→        description = ""
   317→    return {
   318→        "description": description,
   319→        "raw": text,
   320→    }
   321→
   322→
   323→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   324→# Message builder
   325→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   326→
   327→def build_hda_messages(description: str, context: dict | None = None) -> list:
   328→    """Build the initial message list for the HDA design conversation.
   329→
   330→    Parameters
   331→    ----------
   332→    description : str
   333→        The artist's natural language description of the desired HDA.
   334→    context : dict, optional
   335→        Scene context dict. Recognized keys:
   336→
   337→        - ``network`` (str): Current network path (e.g. ``"/obj/geo1"``)
   338→        - ``selected_nodes`` (list[str]): Currently selected node paths
   339→        - ``hip_path`` (str): Current HIP file path
   340→
   341→    Returns
   342→    -------
   343→    list[dict]
   344→        A list of message dicts suitable for the Anthropic API.
   345→    """
   346→    if context is None:
   347→        context = {}
   348→
   349→    network = context.get("network", "/obj")
   350→    selected = context.get("selected_nodes", [])
   351→    hip_path = context.get("hip_path", "")
   352→
   353→    parts = [f"Design and build an HDA: {description}"]
   354→
   355→    if network:
   356→        parts.append(f"Current network context: {network}")
   357→
   358→    if selected:
   359→        parts.append(f"Selected nodes: {', '.join(selected)}")
   360→
   361→    if hip_path:
   362→        parts.append(f"HIP file: {hip_path}")
   363→
   364→    parts.append(
   365→        "Use the hda_package tool to create it. "
   366→        "Save to $HIP/hda/ if no path specified."
   367→    )
   368→
   369→    user_content = "\n".join(parts)
   370→
   371→    return [
   372→        {"role": "user", "content": user_content},
   373→    ]
   374→
   375→
   376→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   377→# Default save path
   378→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   379→
   380→def default_save_path(name: str) -> str:
   381→    """Return a default save path for an HDA file.
   382→
   383→    Tries ``$HIP/hda/<name>.hda`` first (requires ``hou`` module).
   384→    Falls back to ``$HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/hda/<name>.hda``.
   385→    Creates the parent directory if it does not exist.
   386→
   387→    Parameters
   388→    ----------
   389→    name : str
   390→        The operator name (e.g. ``"scatter_on_surface"``).
   391→
   392→    Returns
   393→    -------
   394→    str
   395→        Absolute path to the .hda file.
   396→    """
   397→    hda_dir = None
   398→
   399→    # Try $HIP/hda/ via hou module
   400→    try:
   401→        import hou
   402→        hip = hou.getenv("HIP")
   403→        if hip:
   404→            hda_dir = os.path.join(hip, "hda")
   405→    except ImportError:
   406→        pass
   407→
   408→    # Fallback: $HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/hda/
   409→    if hda_dir is None:
   410→        pref_dir = os.environ.get("HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR", "")
   411→        if not pref_dir:
   412→            # Best-effort default
   413→            pref_dir = os.path.expanduser("~/houdini21.0")
   414→        hda_dir = os.path.join(pref_dir, "hda")
   415→
   416→    # Ensure directory exists
   417→    os.makedirs(hda_dir, exist_ok=True)
   418→
   419→    return os.path.join(hda_dir, f"{name}.hda")
   420→

# SYNAPSE Feature Roadmap — From Co-pilot to Indispensable

> **The Mariana Trench Thesis:** Houdini is the deepest, most powerful DCC
> in existence. The learning curve isn't a wall — it's an ocean. SYNAPSE
> doesn't make the ocean shallow. It gives you a submarine, a sonar, and
> a guide who's been to the bottom and back. The depth is the point.
> We're here to make artists *fearless* in it.

> **Indispensability Test — every feature must hit at least one:**
> 1. "It caught something I would have missed." (Safety net)
> 2. "It taught me something I didn't know." (Knowledge transfer)
> 3. "It did in 30 seconds what takes me 30 minutes." (Velocity)

---

## Sprint Map

```
SPRINT 1: TOOL PARITY (current — MOE Plan v2)
  ├── 102 tool execution from panel
  ├── Memory rename (flat/structured/composed)
  ├── Shot Login (context hydration)
  └── Prompt-to-HDA (/hda)

SPRINT 2: SAFETY NET
  ├── Scene Doctor (/diagnose)
  ├── Render Preflight (/preflight)
  ├── Error Translator
  └── Session Journal

SPRINT 3: KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER
  ├── Explain Mode (/explain)
  ├── Network Trace (/trace)
  ├── VEX Tutor (/vex)
  ├── Recipe Book (/recipes)
  └── First-Time Experience (welcome flow)

SPRINT 4: APEX DEEP DIVE
  ├── APEX Explainer (/apex explain)
  ├── APEX Recipes
  ├── APEX Graph Trace (/apex trace)
  └── KineFX → APEX Migration

SPRINT 5: UI EVOLUTION
  ├── Context Bar v2 (breadcrumbs + memory status)
  ├── Quick Actions (contextual buttons)
  ├── Command Palette (Ctrl+K)
  ├── Split View (chat + results)
  └── Conversation Bookmarks

SPRINT 6: PRODUCTION PIPELINE
  ├── Dependency Map (/deps)
  ├── Performance Profiler (/profile)
  ├── Wedge Analyst (/analyze-wedges)
  ├── Save Shot (/save-shot with auto-triggers)
  └── Cross-Scene Context
```

---

## SPRINT 2: SAFETY NET

**Theme:** "It caught something I would have missed."
**Why first after tool parity:** These features build trust. Before artists
rely on SYNAPSE to *build* things, they need to trust it can *catch* things.
Trust precedes delegation.

---

### SCENE DOCTOR — `/diagnose`

**What it does:** Full health audit of the current scene. Not just listing
problems — offering to fix them.

**Checks (priority order):**

| Check | Severity | Auto-fixable? |
|-------|----------|--------------|
| Missing texture files | Critical | Yes — remap to $JOB paths |
| Broken node references | Critical | Yes — reconnect or flag |
| Unconnected required inputs | Error | Yes — suggest connections |
| Out-of-range parameters | Warning | Yes — clamp to valid range |
| Infinite cook dependencies | Critical | No — explain the cycle |
| Missing camera for render | Error | Yes — create default |
| Zero-area lights | Warning | Yes — set minimum size |
| Empty merge inputs | Warning | Yes — clean up |
| Unused nodes (no output path) | Info | No — just flag |
| Stale cache files | Info | Yes — clear |
| Non-square textures for tiling | Info | No — flag |
| Missing display/render flags | Warning | Yes — set on last node |

**Architecture:**

```
/diagnose
  → gather all nodes in scene (or current network)
  → for each node:
      check inputs connected
      check for cook errors (node.errors())
      check parameter values against metadata ranges
      check file paths exist on disk
  → for render context:
      check camera assignment
      check resolution set
      check output path writable
      check materials bound
  → compile report
  → display in chat with severity icons
  → offer batch fix: "Fix 7 auto-fixable issues?"
```

**Implementation: 2 files**

| File | Agent | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `python/synapse/panel/scene_doctor.py` | INDIA | Diagnostic engine — runs checks, returns structured report |
| Panel integration | JULIET | Wire /diagnose command, display report, handle fix-it flow |

**MOE Prompt — AGENT INDIA (Scene Doctor Engine):**

```
I need you to create a scene diagnostic engine for SYNAPSE.

CONTEXT:
- Repo root: C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE
- SYNAPSE runs inside Houdini 21 with full hou module access
- The panel can execute tools on the main thread via SynapseHandler
- Artists need a /diagnose command that finds and fixes scene problems

YOUR TASK:
Create python/synapse/panel/scene_doctor.py

REQUIREMENTS:

1. Function diagnose_scene(scope: str = "all") -> DiagnosticReport
   scope: "all" | "current_network" | "render" | "materials"

   Returns a DiagnosticReport dataclass:
   @dataclass
   class DiagnosticIssue:
       severity: str     # "critical", "error", "warning", "info"
       category: str     # "missing_file", "broken_ref", "bad_parm", etc.
       node_path: str    # affected node
       message: str      # human-readable description
       fix_available: bool
       fix_description: str  # what the fix would do
       fix_fn: Optional[Callable]  # function that fixes it (called on main thread)

   @dataclass
   class DiagnosticReport:
       issues: List[DiagnosticIssue]
       nodes_checked: int
       time_elapsed: float
       summary: str  # "Found 12 issues: 2 critical, 3 errors, 5 warnings, 2 info"

2. Individual check functions (each returns list of DiagnosticIssue):
   - check_missing_files(nodes) — textures, alembics, file SOPs
   - check_broken_inputs(nodes) — unconnected required inputs
   - check_cook_errors(nodes) — nodes with existing cook errors
   - check_parameter_ranges(nodes) — values outside metadata min/max
   - check_render_readiness() — camera, resolution, output path, materials
   - check_circular_deps(nodes) — infinite cook loops
   - check_unused_nodes(nodes) — nodes with no downstream consumers
   - check_display_flags(network) — missing display/render flags
   - check_empty_merges(nodes) — merge nodes with disconnected inputs

3. Function apply_fixes(issues: List[DiagnosticIssue]) -> dict
   Applies all auto-fixable issues. Returns {fixed: int, failed: int, skipped: int}.
   Wraps everything in an undo group.

4. hou import is required but wrapped in try/except at module level.
   If hou unavailable, diagnose_scene returns empty report.

5. ALL hou calls must be safe for the main thread. Use node.errors(),
   node.inputs(), node.parms(), parm.eval(), etc.
   Do NOT cook nodes — just inspect current state.

6. File existence checks should handle $JOB, $HIP, $HOME variable expansion
   using hou.text.expandString() or hou.expandString().

7. Performance: must complete full scene audit in <5 seconds for 500-node scenes.
   Short-circuit expensive checks on large scenes.

VERIFY:
- Read python/synapse/server/handlers.py for patterns of hou.* usage
- The module will be called from the main thread by the panel
- Run: python -c "from synapse.panel.scene_doctor import DiagnosticReport; print('OK')"
  (Will work outside Houdini for import check — actual diagnosis needs hou)

DO NOT modify existing files. Only create python/synapse/panel/scene_doctor.py
```

---

### RENDER PREFLIGHT — `/preflight`

**What it does:** Pre-render checklist that catches the problems that waste
overnight farm hours. This is the feature pipeline TDs dream about.

**Checks:**

| Check | What It Catches |
|-------|----------------|
| Memory estimation | "This scene will need ~48GB RAM. Your machine has 32GB." |
| Texture resolution audit | "8K texture on a background element 200px in frame. Suggest 1K." |
| Light sampling analysis | "Area light with 1 sample — will be noisy. Suggest 4-16." |
| Motion blur completeness | "Deforming geo on /obj/character but no motion blur enabled." |
| AOV check | "Missing diffuse_direct AOV — Nuke comp will need it." |
| Frame range sanity | "Render set to frame 1-1. Scene has animation to frame 240." |
| Output path | "Output directory doesn't exist / isn't writable." |
| Camera check | "No camera assigned to ROP / camera has zero resolution." |
| Material binding | "3 prims with no material assignment — will render default gray." |
| Subdivision levels | "6 levels of subdivision on background geo. Consider 2-3." |

**Implementation: 1 file**

```
python/synapse/panel/render_preflight.py
```

Follows the same pattern as scene_doctor: structured report, severity levels,
auto-fix where possible. Focused specifically on render pipeline.

---

### ERROR TRANSLATOR

**What it does:** Intercepts Houdini error messages and translates them into
human-readable explanations with suggested fixes.

**This is invisible infrastructure.** No slash command — it activates
automatically when the artist encounters an error and asks SYNAPSE about it,
or when a tool execution returns an error.

**Implementation approach:** A lookup table of common error patterns mapped
to plain-English explanations, plus a fallback that sends the raw error to
Claude with node context for interpretation.

```python
ERROR_PATTERNS = {
    r"SOP_AttribCreate.*invalid group": {
        "explain": "The group field references a group that doesn't exist on the incoming geometry.",
        "suggest": "Check available groups with /inspect on the input node.",
        "auto_fix": None,  # needs user decision
    },
    r"Unable to read file (.+)": {
        "explain": "Houdini can't find the file at {match_1}.",
        "suggest": "Check if the file exists. If it moved, update the path.",
        "auto_fix": "search_for_file",
    },
    r"Cook error.*maximum recursion": {
        "explain": "A node is referencing itself in a loop, causing infinite recursion.",
        "suggest": "Look for circular channel references or SOP dependencies.",
        "auto_fix": None,
    },
}
```

**The fallback is the real power:** When no pattern matches, SYNAPSE sends
the error + node info + network context to Claude and gets a natural language
explanation. Over time, the pattern table grows from what Claude explains.

### SESSION JOURNAL

**What it does:** Automatic, invisible logging of every SYNAPSE action.
Not the full conversation — just the actions and their results.

**Journal entry format:**
```
[14:32:07] Created node /obj/geo1/mountain1 (type: mountain, requested: "add some terrain displacement")
[14:32:08] Set parm /obj/geo1/mountain1/height = 3.5
[14:32:08] Connected /obj/geo1/mountain1 output 0 → /obj/geo1/null1 input 0
[14:33:15] /diagnose: Found 2 warnings (empty merge, missing display flag). Auto-fixed both.
[14:45:02] /preflight: Scene render-ready. Estimated 12GB RAM, 4min/frame on GPU.
[14:50:00] Render started: karma_xpu, frames 1-240, output: $HIP/render/beauty.####.exr
```

**Access via `/journal`** — shows the session log. `/journal search displacement`
finds relevant entries. Journal entries become part of scene memory on save.

**Implementation:** A simple append-only log writer that hooks into tool
execution (ToolExecutor logs after each tool completes) and slash commands.
Stored at `$HIP/claude/journal.log` with ISO timestamps.

## SPRINT 3: KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER

**Theme:** "It taught me something I didn't know."
**Why this sprint:** After trust (Sprint 2), artists start exploring.
This sprint makes SYNAPSE the best teacher Houdini has ever had.

---

### EXPLAIN MODE — `/explain`

**What it does:** Select any node or network, type `/explain`. SYNAPSE reads
everything about it and explains in plain English.

**What it reads:**
- Node type and its documentation
- Current parameter values (not defaults — what's actually set)
- Input connections and what data they carry
- Output data (point count, prim count, attribute list)
- Cook time
- Any errors or warnings
- Position in the network (what's upstream, what's downstream)

**What it produces (example):**

> **mountain1** (Mountain SOP)
>
> This node adds procedural noise displacement to the incoming grid.
> It's pushing vertices up and down based on a noise pattern — think of it
> like crumpling a sheet of paper, but mathematically controlled.
>
> Right now it's set to:
> - Height: 3.5 (how tall the peaks get)
> - Element Size: 2.0 (how wide each mountain — bigger = smoother hills)
> - Roughness: 0.6 (how jagged — 0 is smooth rolling, 1 is sharp peaks)
> - Offset: animated (it's moving over time — that's why the terrain drifts)
>
> It's receiving a 200×200 grid (40,000 points) from grid1 above, and feeding
> into a color SOP below that's painting based on height.
>
> Cook time: 2.3ms — very fast, no concern here.

**The key insight:** This isn't documentation. Documentation tells you what
a Mountain SOP *can* do. SYNAPSE tells you what *this particular one* is
*actually doing* in *your scene*.

**Implementation:**

```
python/synapse/panel/explain_mode.py

Function: explain_node(node_path: str) -> str
  - Get node type info (hou.nodeType.description())
  - Get all non-default parameter values
  - Get input/output geometry stats
  - Get cook time from performance monitor
  - Get errors/warnings
  - Build a structured context dict
  - Send to Claude with a "explain this node for a Houdini artist" prompt
  - Return the explanation

Function: explain_network(network_path: str) -> str
  - List all nodes in order of data flow
  - For each: type, key parms, connections
  - Send to Claude with "explain this network as a data flow"
  - Return the walkthrough
```

---

### NETWORK TRACE — `/trace`

**What it does:** Follows data from the top of a network to the display node,
narrating each transformation.

**Output (example):**
> **Data flow in /obj/geo1:**
>
> 1. **grid1** — Creates a 50×50 polygon grid (2,500 points, 2,401 quads)
> 2. **mountain1** — Displaces Y position with turbulent noise. Peak height: 5.0.
>    Points: 2,500 → 2,500 (no change). New attribute: none. Time: 1.2ms.
> 3. **attribwrangle1** — Custom VEX: colors points by height using a ramp.
>    Reads: @P.y. Writes: @Cd. Points: 2,500. Time: 0.4ms.
> 4. **scatter1** — Distributes 10,000 random points on the surface.
>    Points: 2,500 → 10,000. Inherits: @Cd, @N. Time: 3.1ms.
> 5. **copytopoints1** — Copies tree_geo (input 2: 1,200 pts) onto each scatter point.
>    Points: 10,000 × 1,200 = 12,000,000. ⚠️ This is heavy. Time: 890ms.
>
> **Total: 895ms cook time. Bottleneck: copytopoints1 (99.4%)**

**This is how you learn Houdini.** Not by reading docs — by watching data
flow through a real network with real numbers.

### VEX TUTOR — `/vex`

**Three modes:**

`/vex explain` — Select a wrangle, explains the code line by line with context.

`/vex help {concept}` — Quick reference: `/vex help pcfind` explains the function
with a practical example using the artist's actual geometry.

`/vex write {description}` — "Color points by distance from the center" →
writes the VEX snippet AND explains each line as it writes it.

**Key principle:** Never just give code. Always explain *why* this approach.
"We're using `length(@P)` instead of `distance(@P, {0,0,0})` because
when measuring from origin, length is faster — it skips the subtraction."

**Organized by context, not alphabet:**

```
/recipes               → show categories
/recipes scatter       → scatter techniques (uniform, weighted, Poisson, relaxed)
/recipes volumes       → VDB operations, pyro setups, cloud modeling
/recipes materials     → common material patterns, layered materials, procedurals
/recipes rigging       → KineFX chains, constraints, APEX basics
/recipes rendering     → Karma setups, AOV configs, optimization tricks
/recipes usd           → composition patterns, variant sets, asset structure
/recipes vex           → common wrangle patterns by category
/recipes motion        → motion blur, velocity fields, trail effects
```

**Each recipe has:**
- 1-line description
- Required context (SOPs? LOPs? What inputs?)
- "Build it" action — SYNAPSE creates the network right there
- "Explain it" action — walkthrough of why this approach

**Recipes are extensible.** The artist can `/recipes add "my displacement technique"`
and SYNAPSE saves the current network as a named recipe in project memory.

## SPRINT 4: APEX DEEP DIVE

**Theme:** Make APEX approachable. It's the future of Houdini rigging and
almost nobody understands it yet. First-mover advantage for SYNAPSE.

---

### APEX EXPLAINER — `/apex explain`

APEX introduces concepts that don't exist anywhere else in Houdini:

| Concept | What Artists Think | What It Actually Is |
|---------|-------------------|-------------------|
| APEX Graph | "Some kind of VOP network?" | An execution program stored as geometry |
| Packed Folder | "Packed geo?" | A container for rig components — like a namespace |
| Invoke SOP | "Runs something?" | Executes an APEX graph on input geometry |
| Rig Logic vs Rig Execution | "???" | Logic = how to build the rig. Execution = evaluating it per frame. |
| APEX Autorig | "Magic?" | A set of pre-built APEX graphs for standard rig tasks |
| Character Definition | "A rig?" | A structured packed folder hierarchy that defines rig structure |

`/apex explain` on any APEX node gives the Mariana Trench guide explanation:

> **apex::invoke1** (APEX Invoke)
>
> Think of this as a "run program" button. The "program" is an APEX graph
> stored as packed geometry coming in from input 1. That graph describes
> a sequence of operations — like a VEX wrangle, but visual and graph-based.
>
> Right now it's running an FK solver graph on the skeleton coming from
> input 0. The graph reads joint transforms, applies FK rotations from
> control channels, and writes the result back to the skeleton.
>
> The key mental model: APEX graphs are *programs stored as geometry*.
> They travel with your scene, they're inspectable, and they compose.

---

### APEX RECIPES

Production-ready APEX setups buildable via /hda or direct execution:

| Recipe | What It Builds |
|--------|---------------|
| FK Chain | Curve → joints → FK controls → APEX graph |
| IK Chain | Curve → joints → IK solver → pole vector control |
| FK/IK Blend | Combined chain with blend control |
| Autorig Character | T-pose → APEX Autorig → full character rig |
| Facial Rig | Points → blend shapes → APEX control graph |
| Muscle System | Joints → muscle primitives → deform |
| Custom Deformer | Input geo → APEX deformer graph → output |
| KineFX Conversion | Existing KineFX rig → equivalent APEX setup |

Each recipe includes:
- The node network to build
- An `/explain` walkthrough of each step
- Key parameter descriptions
- "What to tweak first" guide

---

### APEX GRAPH TRACE — `/apex trace`

APEX graphs are hard to debug because execution is opaque.

`/apex trace` on an Invoke node:
1. Reads the APEX graph from packed geometry
2. Lists all nodes in execution order
3. For each node: what it computes, what it reads, what it writes
4. Highlights the critical path (slowest evaluation chain)
5. Shows data flow between rig components

This is tooling that *doesn't exist yet*. SideFX has basic graph visualization
but no step-by-step narrated trace. SYNAPSE would be the first.

## Implementation Priority Guide

**If you have 1 sprint after tool parity:** Sprint 2 (Safety Net).
Trust precedes everything.

**If you have 2 sprints:** Sprint 2 + Sprint 3 (Knowledge Transfer).
Safety + learning = artists who are confident AND growing.

**If you're targeting a demo:** Sprint 2's /diagnose + Sprint 3's /explain +
Sprint 1's /hda. Those three in a 60-second video tell the whole story:
"SYNAPSE catches your mistakes, teaches you new things, and builds what you ask for."

**If you're targeting studios:** Sprint 6 (Production Pipeline) becomes
Sprint 2. Studios care about /deps, /profile, and save-shot more than
/explain. Reorder based on audience.

**The APEX sprint** is a market differentiator. Nobody is doing AI-assisted

I need you to create a render preflight checker for SYNAPSE.

CONTEXT:
- Repo root: C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE
- SYNAPSE runs inside Houdini 21 with full hou module access
- Artists need a /preflight command that catches render problems BEFORE
  wasting hours on farm renders
- This module runs on the main thread inside Houdini

YOUR TASK:
Create python/synapse/panel/render_preflight.py

REQUIREMENTS:

1. Dataclasses:

   @dataclass
   class PreflightCheck:
       name: str          # short identifier: "camera", "output_path", etc.
       status: str        # "pass", "fail", "warn"
       message: str       # human-readable result
       detail: str        # additional info (empty if not needed)
       fix_available: bool
       fix_fn: Optional[Callable]

   @dataclass
   class PreflightReport:
       checks: list       # List[PreflightCheck]
       render_node: str   # path to the ROP/Karma node being checked
       ready: bool        # True only if zero "fail" checks
       summary: str       # "Preflight: 8/10 passed, 1 warning, 1 failure"

2. Main function: run_preflight(render_node: str = "") -> PreflightReport
   If render_node is empty, auto-detect:
   - Look for Karma LOP in /stage (prefer the one with display flag)
   - Fall back to first ROP in /out
   - If nothing found, return report with single "fail": "No render node found"

3. Individual checks (each returns PreflightCheck):

   a) check_camera(render_node) — Is a camera assigned? Does it exist?
      For Karma LOPs: check the "camera" parm.
      For ROPs: check "camera" parm.
      Fail if no camera or camera path doesn't resolve to a node.
      Fix: None (needs user to pick camera).

   b) check_output_path(render_node) — Is output path set? Does the
      directory exist? Is it writable?
      For Karma LOPs: check "picture" parm.
      For ROPs: check "outputimage" or "picture" parm.
      Fail if empty. Warn if directory doesn't exist.
      Fix: Create directory if it doesn't exist.

   c) check_resolution(render_node) — Is resolution set to something
      reasonable? Warn if <100 or >8192 on either axis.
      Check "resolutionx" and "resolutiony" or "res" parm.
      Pass if in normal range.

   d) check_frame_range(render_node) — What's the frame range?
      Warn if it's a single frame but the scene has animation
      (check hou.playbar.frameRange() vs render range).
      Info-level note showing the configured range.

   e) check_materials(render_node) — For Solaris renders, traverse the
      USD stage and find prims with no material binding.
      Use the stage from the Karma LOP: node.stage().
      Warn if unbound geometry prims found.
      Keep it fast: only check leaf Mesh/BasisCurves prims, limit to first 100.

   f) check_lights(render_node) — Are there any lights in the scene?
      For Solaris: check for UsdLux light prims on the stage.
      For /obj renders: check for light objects.
      Fail if zero lights.
      Warn if only a single light (probably needs fill/rim).

   g) check_memory_estimate(render_node) — Rough estimate based on:
      - Total geometry point count across all visible prims
      - Texture file sizes (sum of referenced textures)
      - Subdivision levels
      Report as info with estimate: "Estimated ~XGB memory usage"
      Warn if estimate > 80% of system RAM.
      Use psutil if available, otherwise assume 64GB.

   h) check_motion_blur(render_node) — If motion blur is enabled,
      check that velocity attributes exist on animated geometry.
      If disabled but scene has fast-moving objects, suggest enabling it.
      This is best-effort — just check if xform animation exists on key objects.

   i) check_render_engine(render_node) — Report which engine (CPU/XPU).
      Warn if CPU on a scene that could benefit from XPU.
      Info-level, not a blocker.

4. Function format_preflight_html(report: PreflightReport) -> str
   Formats as HTML for the panel's QTextEdit.
   Use checkmark/cross/warning icons with colors.
   Show render node path at top.
   Show summary: "Ready to render" (green) or "N issues to fix" (red).
   Group: failures first, then warnings, then passes.

5. hou import wrapped in try/except. If unavailable, return empty report.
   Each check function should catch its own exceptions — one check
   failing should not prevent others from running.

6. For USD stage access: use node.stage() on LOP nodes. This returns
   a pxr.Usd.Stage. Check prims via stage.Traverse().
   Wrap pxr imports in try/except.

7. Performance: preflight should complete in <3 seconds. The material
   and memory checks should have early-exit limits (first 100 prims,
   first 50 textures).

VERIFY:
- Read python/synapse/server/handlers.py to see patterns of hou.* and stage access
- Read python/synapse/panel/scene_doctor.py for the dataclass/report pattern (similar structure)
- Run: python -c "from synapse.panel.render_preflight import PreflightReport, run_preflight; print('Import OK')"

I need you to create a render preflight checker for SYNAPSE.

CONTEXT:
- Repo root: C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE
- SYNAPSE runs inside Houdini 21 with full hou module access
- Artists need a /preflight command that catches render problems BEFORE
  wasting hours on farm renders
- This module runs on the main thread inside Houdini

YOUR TASK:
Create python/synapse/panel/render_preflight.py

REQUIREMENTS:

1. Dataclasses:

   @dataclass
   class PreflightCheck:
       name: str          # short identifier: "camera", "output_path", etc.
       status: str        # "pass", "fail", "warn"
       message: str       # human-readable result
       detail: str        # additional info (empty if not needed)
       fix_available: bool
       fix_fn: Optional[Callable]

   @dataclass
   class PreflightReport:
       checks: list       # List[PreflightCheck]
       render_node: str   # path to the ROP/Karma node being checked
       ready: bool        # True only if zero "fail" checks
       summary: str       # "Preflight: 8/10 passed, 1 warning, 1 failure"

2. Main function: run_preflight(render_node: str = "") -> PreflightReport
   If render_node is empty, auto-detect:
   - Look for Karma LOP in /stage (prefer the one with display flag)
   - Fall back to first ROP in /out
   - If nothing found, return report with single "fail": "No render node found"

3. Individual checks (each returns PreflightCheck):

   a) check_camera(render_node) — Is a camera assigned? Does it exist?
      For Karma LOPs: check the "camera" parm.
      For ROPs: check "camera" parm.
      Fail if no camera or camera path doesn't resolve to a node.
      Fix: None (needs user to pick camera).

   b) check_output_path(render_node) — Is output path set? Does the
      directory exist? Is it writable?
      For Karma LOPs: check "picture" parm.
      For ROPs: check "outputimage" or "picture" parm.
      Fail if empty. Warn if directory doesn't exist.
      Fix: Create directory if it doesn't exist.

   c) check_resolution(render_node) — Is resolution set to something
      reasonable? Warn if <100 or >8192 on either axis.
      Check "resolutionx" and "resolutiony" or "res" parm.
      Pass if in normal range.

   d) check_frame_range(render_node) — What's the frame range?
      Warn if it's a single frame but the scene has animation
      (check hou.playbar.frameRange() vs render range).
      Info-level note showing the configured range.

   e) check_materials(render_node) — For Solaris renders, traverse the
      USD stage and find prims with no material binding.
      Use the stage from the Karma LOP: node.stage().
      Warn if unbound geometry prims found.
      Keep it fast: only check leaf Mesh/BasisCurves prims, limit to first 100.

   f) check_lights(render_node) — Are there any lights in the scene?
      For Solaris: check for UsdLux light prims on the stage.
      For /obj renders: check for light objects.
      Fail if zero lights.
      Warn if only a single light (probably needs fill/rim).

   g) check_memory_estimate(render_node) — Rough estimate based on:
      - Total geometry point count across all visible prims
      - Texture file sizes (sum of referenced textures)
      - Subdivision levels
      Report as info with estimate: "Estimated ~XGB memory usage"
      Warn if estimate > 80% of system RAM.
      Use psutil if available, otherwise assume 64GB.

   h) check_motion_blur(render_node) — If motion blur is enabled,
      check that velocity attributes exist on animated geometry.
      If disabled but scene has fast-moving objects, suggest enabling it.
      This is best-effort — just check if xform animation exists on key objects.

   i) check_render_engine(render_node) — Report which engine (CPU/XPU).
      Warn if CPU on a scene that could benefit from XPU.
      Info-level, not a blocker.

4. Function format_preflight_html(report: PreflightReport) -> str
   Formats as HTML for the panel's QTextEdit.
   Use checkmark/cross/warning icons with colors.
   Show render node path at top.
   Show summary: "Ready to render" (green) or "N issues to fix" (red).
   Group: failures first, then warnings, then passes.

5. hou import wrapped in try/except. If unavailable, return empty report.
   Each check function should catch its own exceptions — one check
   failing should not prevent others from running.

6. For USD stage access: use node.stage() on LOP nodes. This returns
   a pxr.Usd.Stage. Check prims via stage.Traverse().
   Wrap pxr imports in try/except.

7. Performance: preflight should complete in <3 seconds. The material
   and memory checks should have early-exit limits (first 100 prims,
   first 50 textures).

VERIFY:
- Read python/synapse/server/handlers.py to see patterns of hou.* and stage access
- Read python/synapse/panel/scene_doctor.py for the dataclass/report pattern (similar structure)
- Run: python -c "from synapse.panel.render_preflight import PreflightReport, run_preflight; print('Import OK')"

data.prompt:
I need you to create an error translator for SYNAPSE.

CONTEXT:
- Repo root: C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE
- SYNAPSE runs inside Houdini 21
- When Houdini produces cryptic error messages, artists shouldn't have to
  decode them alone. The error translator intercepts errors and provides
  plain-English explanations with suggested fixes.
- This is invisible infrastructure — it activates when tools fail or when
  the artist asks about an error. No slash command needed.

YOUR TASK:
Create python/synapse/panel/error_translator.py

REQUIREMENTS:

1. Constant ERROR_PATTERNS -> list of dicts
   Each entry:
   {
       "pattern": r"regex pattern",    # compiled at module level
       "category": str,                # "file_not_found", "cook_error", "vex_error", etc.
       "explain": str,                 # plain-English explanation (may use {match_N} for groups)
       "suggest": str,                 # suggested action
       "severity": str,                # "critical", "error", "warning"
   }

   Include at least 20 patterns covering common Houdini errors:

   File/Path errors:
   - "Unable to read file (.+)" — file not found
   - "Cannot find asset (.+)" — missing HDA
   - "Error loading texture (.+)" — texture load failure
   - "Permission denied: (.+)" — file permission issue

   Cook errors:
   - "Cook error in (.+)" — generic cook failure
   - "Maximum recursion depth exceeded" — circular dependency
   - "SOP cook error: (.+)" — SOP-specific cook failure
   - "Error cooking DOP" — simulation cook error

   VEX errors:
   - "VEX error: (.+)" — generic VEX error
   - "Syntax error, unexpected (.+)" — VEX syntax error
   - "Cannot find function (.+)" — undefined VEX function
   - "Type mismatch" — VEX type error
   - "Possible loss of precision" — VEX precision warning

   USD/Solaris errors:
   - "Failed to compose prim (.+)" — USD composition error
   - "Cannot resolve asset path (.+)" — USD asset resolution failure
   - "Invalid layer (.+)" — corrupt or missing USD layer

   Render errors:
   - "Karma: (.+)" — Karma render error
   - "Out of memory" — OOM during render
   - "License not available" — licensing issue

   General:
   - "Node (.+) is not installed" — missing node type
   - "Invalid group name (.+)" — bad group reference

2. Function translate_error(error_text: str) -> dict or None
   Tries each pattern against the error text (case-insensitive).
   On first match, returns:
   {
       "original": str,       # the raw error text
       "category": str,
       "explanation": str,    # with regex groups substituted
       "suggestion": str,     # with regex groups substituted
       "severity": str,
       "matched_pattern": str # the pattern name/category for logging
   }
   Returns None if no pattern matches.

3. Function translate_tool_error(tool_name: str, error_text: str) -> str
   Wraps translate_error with tool-specific context.
   Returns a formatted plain-English string like:
   "The {tool_name} tool hit a snag: {explanation}. {suggestion}"
   If no pattern matches, returns a generic:
   "The {tool_name} tool returned an error: {error_text}"
   Keeps the SYNAPSE coaching tone — collaborative, not clinical.

4. Function get_error_context(node_path: str) -> dict
   Gathers context about a node that has errors, for sending to Claude
   when no pattern matches (the fallback path).
   Returns:
   {
       "node_path": str,
       "node_type": str,
       "errors": list,          # node.errors()
       "warnings": list,        # node.warnings()
       "input_types": list,     # types of connected input nodes
       "parm_count": int,
       "has_expression": bool,  # any parms with expressions
       "cook_count": int,
   }
   hou import is try/excepted. Returns minimal dict if hou unavailable.

5. Function format_translation_html(translation: dict) -> str
   Formats a translation result as HTML for the panel's chat display.
   Use the coaching tone:
   - "We hit a snag" not "Error occurred"
   - "Looks like..." not "Error:"
   - Severity-colored left border (same pattern as tool_status)
   - Suggestion in a lighter color below the explanation

6. Compile all regex patterns at module level (re.compile with re.IGNORECASE).
   Pattern matching should be fast — this may be called on every tool error.

7. The patterns list should be ordered by specificity — more specific patterns
   first, generic fallbacks last. translate_error returns on FIRST match.

8. No hou import at module level. get_error_context imports hou lazily.
   translate_error and translate_tool_error work without hou.

VERIFY:
- Run: python -c "
from synapse.panel.error_translator import translate_error, translate_tool_error
r = translate_error('Unable to read file /path/to/texture.exr')
print(r['explanation'])
print(r['suggestion'])
r2 = translate_tool_error('houdini_set_parm', 'VEX error: Syntax error, unexpected token')
print(r2)
print('Pattern count:', len(__import__('synapse.panel.error_translator', fromlist=['ERROR_PATTERNS']).ERROR_PATTERNS))
"

DO NOT modify existing files. Only create python/synapse/panel/error_translator.py

  plain-English explanations with suggested fixes.
- This is invisible infrastructure — it activates when tools fail or when
  the artist asks about an error. No slash command needed.

YOUR TASK:
Create python/synapse/panel/error_translator.py

REQUIREMENTS:

1. Constant ERROR_PATTERNS -> list of dicts
   Each entry:
   {
       "pattern": r"regex pattern",    # compiled at module level
       "category": str,                # "file_not_found", "cook_error", "vex_error", etc.
       "explain": str,                 # plain-English explanation (may use {match_N} for groups)
       "suggest": str,                 # suggested action
       "severity": str,                # "critical", "error", "warning"
   }

   Include at least 20 patterns covering common Houdini errors:

   File/Path errors:
   - "Unable to read file (.+)" — file not found
   - "Cannot find asset (.+)" — missing HDA
   - "Error loading texture (.+)" — texture load failure
   - "Permission denied: (.+)" — file permission issue

   Cook errors:
   - "Cook error in (.+)" — generic cook failure
   - "Maximum recursion depth exceeded" — circular dependency
   - "SOP cook error: (.+)" — SOP-specific cook failure
   - "Error cooking DOP" — simulation cook error

   VEX errors:
   - "VEX error: (.+)" — generic VEX error
   - "Syntax error, unexpected (.+)" — VEX syntax error
   - "Cannot find function (.+)" — undefined VEX function
   - "Type mismatch" — VEX type error
   - "Possible loss of precision" — VEX precision warning

   USD/Solaris errors:
   - "Failed to compose prim (.+)" — USD composition error
   - "Cannot resolve asset path (.+)" — USD asset resolution failure
   - "Invalid layer (.+)" — corrupt or missing USD layer

   Render errors:
   - "Karma: (.+)" — Karma render error
   - "Out of memory" — OOM during render
   - "License not available" — licensing issue

   General:
   - "Node (.+) is not installed" — missing node type
   - "Invalid group name (.+)" — bad group reference

2. Function translate_error(error_text: str) -> dict or None
   Tries each pattern against the error text (case-insensitive).
   On first match, returns:
   {
       "original": str,       # the raw error text
       "category": str,
       "explanation": str,    # with regex groups substituted
       "suggestion": str,     # with regex groups substituted
       "severity": str,
       "matched_pattern": str # the pattern name/category for logging
   }
   Returns None if no pattern matches.

3. Function translate_tool_error(tool_name: str, error_text: str) -> str
   Wraps translate_error with tool-specific context.
   Returns a formatted plain-English string like:
   "The {tool_name} tool hit a snag: {explanation}. {suggestion}"
   If no pattern matches, returns a generic:
   "The {tool_name} tool returned an error: {error_text}"
   Keeps the SYNAPSE coaching tone — collaborative, not clinical.

4. Function get_error_context(node_path: str) -> dict
   Gathers context about a node that has errors, for sending to Claude
   when no pattern matches (the fallback path).
   Returns:
   {
       "node_path": str,
       "node_type": str,
       "errors": list,          # node.errors()
       "warnings": list,        # node.warnings()
       "input_types": list,     # types of connected input nodes
       "parm_count": int,
       "has_expression": bool,  # any parms with expressions
       "cook_count": int,
   }
   hou import is try/excepted. Returns minimal dict if hou unavailable.

5. Function format_translation_html(translation: dict) -> str
   Formats a translation result as HTML for the panel's chat display.
   Use the coaching tone:
   - "We hit a snag" not "Error occurred"
   - "Looks like..." not "Error:"
   - Severity-colored left border (same pattern as tool_status)
   - Suggestion in a lighter color below the explanation

6. Compile all regex patterns at module level (re.compile with re.IGNORECASE).
   Pattern matching should be fast — this may be called on every tool error.

7. The patterns list should be ordered by specificity — more specific patterns
   first, generic fallbacks last. translate_error returns on FIRST match.

8. No hou import at module level. get_error_context imports hou lazily.
   translate_error and translate_tool_error work without hou.

VERIFY:
- Run: python -c "
from synapse.panel.error_translator import translate_error, translate_tool_error
r = translate_error('Unable to read file /path/to/texture.exr')
print(r['explanation'])
print(r['suggestion'])
r2 = translate_tool_error('houdini_set_parm', 'VEX error: Syntax error, unexpected token')
print(r2)
print('Pattern count:', len(__import__('synapse.panel.error_translator', fromlist=['ERROR_PATTERNS']).ERROR_PATTERNS))
"

DO NOT modify existing files. Only create python/synapse/panel/error_translator.py

1→"""
     2→Main-Thread Tool Executor -- Qt signal/slot bridge for Houdini panel.
     3→
     4→The Claude API worker runs on a QThread and cannot call hou.* directly.
     5→This module provides a ToolRequest + ToolExecutor pair that bridges the gap:
     6→
     7→  1. Worker creates a ToolRequest (with a threading.Event)
     8→  2. Worker emits a Qt signal carrying the request
     9→  3. Qt's AutoConnection delivers the signal to ToolExecutor on the main thread
    10→  4. ToolExecutor dispatches through SynapseHandler (which calls hou.*)
    11→  5. ToolExecutor sets request.result/error and fires request.done
    12→  6. Worker's request.done.wait() unblocks
    13→
    14→All hou.* calls happen on the main thread. The worker never touches hou.
    15→"""
    16→
    17→from __future__ import annotations
    18→
    19→import logging
    20→import threading
    21→import time
    22→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    23→from typing import Any, Optional
    24→
    25→try:
    26→    from PySide6 import QtCore
    27→except ImportError:
    28→    from PySide2 import QtCore
    29→
    30→from .tool_bridge import get_tool_dispatch
    31→
    32→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    33→
    34→
    35→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    36→# ToolRequest -- data object shared between worker thread and main thread
    37→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    38→
    39→@dataclass
    40→class ToolRequest:
    41→    """Request object passed from worker thread to main-thread executor.
    42→
    43→    The worker creates this, emits it via signal, then calls
    44→    ``done.wait(timeout=30.0)`` to block until the executor finishes.
    45→
    46→    Attributes:
    47→        tool_use_id: The ``id`` from the Anthropic API tool_use content block.
    48→        tool_name:   MCP tool name (e.g. ``"create_node"``).
    49→        tool_input:  Tool arguments dict from the API.
    50→        result:      Set by executor on success (response.data).
    51→        error:       Set by executor on failure (error message string).
    52→        done:        Threading event -- set by executor when processing is complete.
    53→    """
    54→    tool_use_id: str
    55→    tool_name: str
    56→    tool_input: dict
    57→    result: Any = field(default=None, repr=False)
    58→    error: Optional[str] = None
    59→    done: threading.Event = field(default_factory=threading.Event, repr=False)

input.prompt:
I need you to create a session journal for SYNAPSE.

CONTEXT:
- Repo root: C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE
- SYNAPSE runs inside Houdini 21
- Every tool execution and slash command should be logged automatically
- The journal is append-only, stored at $HIP/claude/journal.log
- Artists can search it with /journal, and it feeds into scene memory

YOUR TASK:
Create python/synapse/panel/session_journal.py

REQUIREMENTS:

1. Class SessionJournal:

   __init__(self, log_dir: str = "")
   - If log_dir empty, try to resolve from hou.hipFile.path() → dirname/claude/
   - If hou unavailable, use a temp directory
   - Create the log directory if it doesn't exist
   - Open/create journal.log file path (don't keep file handle open)
   - Store session start time

   log_tool(self, tool_name: str, tool_input: dict, result: Any, error: str = None, duration_ms: int = 0)
   - Logs a tool execution. Format:
     [HH:MM:SS] TOOL tool_name: brief_summary (duration_ms ms)
     Brief summary should be smart — not dump the whole input dict, but extract
     the key info:
     - create_node: "Created {type} at {path}"
     - set_parm: "Set {path}/{parm} = {value}"
     - connect_nodes: "Connected {src} → {dst}"
     - execute_python: "Ran Python snippet ({n} chars)"
     - For others: first 80 chars of JSON input

   log_command(self, command: str, result_summary: str = "")
   - Logs a slash command execution. Format:
     [HH:MM:SS] CMD {command}: {result_summary}

   log_event(self, event_type: str, message: str)
   - Generic event log. Format:
     [HH:MM:SS] {EVENT_TYPE} {message}
   - Used for: shot_login, diagnosis results, preflight results, errors

   search(self, query: str, limit: int = 50) -> list
   - Search journal entries matching the query string (case-insensitive).
   - Returns list of matching lines, most recent first.
   - If query is empty, returns the last `limit` entries.

   get_session_summary(self) -> str
   - Returns a brief summary of the current session:
     "Session: {duration}min, {tool_count} tools, {cmd_count} commands"
   - Reads from in-memory counters (don't re-parse the file).

   get_entries(self, limit: int = 50) -> list
   - Returns the last N entries from the journal file.
   - Reads from the file (not in-memory) for persistence across panel restarts.

2. Function format_journal_html(entries: list, query: str = "") -> str
   Formats journal entries as HTML for the panel's QTextEdit.
   - Monospace font for log entries
   - Highlight matching query terms in entries (bold or color)
   - Show entry count and any search query at the top
   - If query provided: "Found N entries matching '{query}'"
   - If no query: "Last N entries (session: {summary})"

3. Module-level singleton pattern:
   _journal_instance: Optional[SessionJournal] = None

   def get_journal(log_dir: str = "") -> SessionJournal:
       """Get or create the singleton journal instance."""
       global _journal_instance
       if _journal_instance is None:
           _journal_instance = SessionJournal(log_dir)
       return _journal_instance

4. File I/O:
   - Append to journal.log on each log call (open, append, close — don't keep handle)
   - Use encoding='utf-8' on all file operations
   - Each entry is a single line (no multi-line entries)
   - File format is plain text, one entry per line
   - Handle file I/O errors gracefully (log to stderr, don't crash)

5. In-memory counters:
   - self._tool_count: int = 0
   - self._cmd_count: int = 0
   - self._event_count: int = 0
   - self._start_time: float = time.time()
   Incremented on each log call. Used for get_session_summary().

6. Tool summarization — _summarize_tool(tool_name, tool_input, result, error):
   Returns a concise one-line summary. Pattern-match on common tool names:

   TOOL_SUMMARIES = {
       "houdini_create_node": lambda inp, res, err: f"Created {inp.get('type','')} at {inp.get('path','')}",
       "houdini_set_parm": lambda inp, res, err: f"Set {inp.get('path','')}/{inp.get('parm','')} = {inp.get('value','')}",
       "houdini_connect_nodes": lambda inp, res, err: f"Connected {inp.get('source','')} → {inp.get('destination','')}",
       "houdini_delete_node": lambda inp, res, err: f"Deleted {inp.get('path','')}",
       "houdini_execute_python": lambda inp, res, err: f"Ran Python ({len(inp.get('code',''))} chars)",
       "houdini_execute_vex": lambda inp, res, err: f"Ran VEX on {inp.get('node_path','')}",
       "houdini_render": lambda inp, res, err: f"Rendered {inp.get('rop_path','')}",
       "houdini_hda_package": lambda inp, res, err: f"Packaged HDA '{inp.get('name','')}'",
   }

   For unknown tools: truncate json.dumps(tool_input) to 80 chars.
   If error: append " [FAILED: {error[:60]}]"

7. hou import is try/excepted. Journal works without hou (uses provided log_dir or temp).

8. Thread safety: use a threading.Lock around file writes. The journal
   may be written from the main thread (tool executor) and read from
   the panel's UI thread.

VERIFY:
- Run: python -c "
from synapse.panel.session_journal import SessionJournal, get_journal, format_journal_html
j = SessionJournal()
j.log_tool('houdini_create_node', {'type': 'geo', 'path': '/obj'}, {'node_path': '/obj/geo1'})
j.log_command('/diagnose', 'Found 3 issues')
j.log_event('LOGIN', 'Shot login: project=flat, scene=flat')
entries = j.get_entries()
print(f'{len(entries)} entries')
print(entries[0])
print(j.get_session_summary())
html = format_journal_html(entries)
print(f'HTML length: {len(html)} chars')
"

DO NOT modify existing files. Only create python/synapse/panel/session_journal.py

CONTEXT:
- Repo root: C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE
- SYNAPSE runs inside Houdini 21 with full hou module access
- The panel can execute tools on the main thread via SynapseHandler
- Artists need a /diagnose command that finds and fixes scene problems
- This module will be called from the panel's main thread

YOUR TASK:
Create python/synapse/panel/scene_doctor.py

REQUIREMENTS:

1. Dataclasses:

   @dataclass
   class DiagnosticIssue:
       severity: str     # "critical", "error", "warning", "info"
       category: str     # "missing_file", "broken_ref", "bad_parm", "cook_error", etc.
       node_path: str    # affected node
       message: str      # human-readable description
       fix_available: bool
       fix_description: str  # what the fix would do (empty if no fix)
       fix_fn: Optional[Callable]  # function that fixes it (called on main thread)

   @dataclass
   class DiagnosticReport:
       issues: list       # List[DiagnosticIssue]
       nodes_checked: int
       time_elapsed: float
       summary: str  # "Found 12 issues: 2 critical, 3 errors, 5 warnings, 2 info"

2. Main function: diagnose_scene(scope: str = "all") -> DiagnosticReport
   scope: "all" | "current_network" | "render" | "materials"

   Gathers nodes based on scope, runs all checks, compiles report.
   Times itself. Builds summary string from issue counts by severity.

3. Individual check functions (each returns list of DiagnosticIssue):

   a) check_missing_files(nodes) — Inspect file-referencing parameters:
      Look for parms with type hou.parmTemplateType.String that have
      file_type tags or names like "file", "filepath", "sopoutput", "filename".
      Expand the value with hou.text.expandString() and check os.path.exists().
      Fix: None (needs user to provide correct path).

   b) check_broken_inputs(nodes) — For each node, check if required inputs
      are connected. Use node.inputConnections() and compare against
      node.type().minNumInputs(). Skip nodes with 0 required inputs.
      Fix: None (needs user decision on what to connect).

   c) check_cook_errors(nodes) — Call node.errors() and node.warnings()
      on each node. Report errors as "error" severity, warnings as "warning".
      Fix: None (underlying cause varies).

   d) check_parameter_ranges(nodes) — For float/int parms, check if
      parmTemplate has min/max set (via .minValue(), .maxValue()) and
      if current value is outside. Only check parms where minIsStrict()
      or maxIsStrict() is True.
      Fix: lambda that clamps the value to the valid range.

   e) check_render_readiness() — Check the render pipeline:
      - Find camera nodes. If none in /obj or /stage, report error.
      - Find ROP nodes in /out. Check if they have valid output paths.
      - For Karma LOPs in /stage: check camera parm is set.
      - Check output directory exists and is writable.
      Fix: Create default camera if missing.

   f) check_display_flags(network_path) — Check if any node in the
      network has its display flag set. If no display flag in a SOP
      network, report warning.
      Fix: Set display flag on the last node in the chain.

   g) check_empty_merges(nodes) — Find merge nodes where some inputs
      are disconnected (gaps in input connections).
      Fix: None (informational).

   h) check_unused_nodes(nodes) — Nodes with no output connections
      AND no display/render flag AND not a ROP. These are "orphans".
      Severity: info. No fix (just flagging).

4. Function apply_fixes(issues: list) -> dict
   Applies all auto-fixable issues (where fix_fn is not None).
   Wraps everything in hou.undos.group("SYNAPSE Scene Doctor Fixes").
   Returns {"fixed": int, "failed": int, "skipped": int}.
   Catches exceptions per-fix so one failure doesn't block others.

5. Function format_report_html(report: DiagnosticReport) -> str
   Formats the report as HTML for display in the panel's QTextEdit.
   Use severity-colored icons:
   - critical: red ✗
   - error: orange ✗
   - warning: yellow ⚠
   - info: gray ℹ

   Group issues by severity (critical first).

I need you to create an error translator for SYNAPSE.

CONTEXT:
- Repo root: C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE
- SYNAPSE runs inside Houdini 21
- When Houdini produces cryptic error messages, artists shouldn't have to
  decode them alone. The error translator intercepts errors and provides
  plain-English explanations with suggested fixes.
- This is invisible infrastructure — it activates when tools fail or when
  the artist asks about an error. No slash command needed.

YOUR TASK:
Create python/synapse/panel/error_translator.py

REQUIREMENTS:

1. Constant ERROR_PATTERNS -> list of dicts
   Each entry:
   {
       "pattern": r"regex pattern",    # compiled at module level
       "category": str,                # "file_not_found", "cook_error", "vex_error", etc.
       "explain": str,                 # plain-English explanation (may use {match_N} for groups)
       "suggest": str,                 # suggested action
       "severity": str,                # "critical", "error", "warning"
   }

   Include at least 20 patterns covering common Houdini errors:

   File/Path errors:
   - "Unable to read file (.+)" — file not found
   - "Cannot find asset (.+)" — missing HDA
   - "Error loading texture (.+)" — texture load failure
   - "Permission denied: (.+)" — file permission issue

   Cook errors:
   - "Cook error in (.+)" — generic cook failure
   - "Maximum recursion depth exceeded" — circular dependency
   - "SOP cook error: (.+)" — SOP-specific cook failure
   - "Error cooking DOP" — simulation cook error

   VEX errors:
   - "VEX error: (.+)" — generic VEX error
   - "Syntax error, unexpected (.+)" — VEX syntax error
   - "Cannot find function (.+)" — undefined VEX function
   - "Type mismatch" — VEX type error
   - "Possible loss of precision" — VEX precision warning

   USD/Solaris errors:
   - "Failed to compose prim (.+)" — USD composition error
   - "Cannot resolve asset path (.+)" — USD asset resolution failure
   - "Invalid layer (.+)" — corrupt or missing USD layer

   Render errors:
   - "Karma: (.+)" — Karma render error
   - "Out of memory" — OOM during render
   - "License not available" — licensing issue

   General:
   - "Node (.+) is not installed" — missing node type
   - "Invalid group name (.+)" — bad group reference

2. Function translate_error(error_text: str) -> dict or None
   Tries each pattern against the error text (case-insensitive).
   On first match, returns:
   {
       "original": str,       # the raw error text
       "category": str,
       "explanation": str,    # with regex groups substituted
       "suggestion": str,     # with regex groups substituted
       "severity": str,
       "matched_pattern": str # the pattern name/category for logging
   }
   Returns None if no pattern matches.

3. Function translate_tool_error(tool_name: str, error_text: str) -> str
   Wraps translate_error with tool-specific context.
   Returns a formatted plain-English string like:
   "The {tool_name} tool hit a snag: {explanation}. {suggestion}"
   If no pattern matches, returns a generic:
   "The {tool_name} tool returned an error: {error_text}"
   Keeps the SYNAPSE coaching tone — collaborative, not clinical.

4. Function get_error_context(node_path: str) -> dict
   Gathers context about a node that has errors, for sending to Claude
   when no pattern matches (the fallback path).
   Returns:
   {
       "node_path": str,
       "node_type": str,
       "errors": list,          # node.errors()
       "warnings": list,        # node.warnings()
       "input_types": list,     # types of connected input nodes
       "parm_count": int,
       "has_expression": bool,  # any parms with expressions
       "cook_count": int,
   }
   hou import is try/excepted. Returns minimal dict if hou unavailable.

5. Function format_translation_html(translation: dict) -> str
   Formats a translation result as HTML for the panel's chat display.
   Use the coaching tone:
   - "We hit a snag" not "Error occurred"
   - "Looks like..." not "Error:"
   - Severity-colored left border (same pattern as tool_status)
   - Suggestion in a lighter color below the explanation

6. Compile all regex patterns at module level (re.compile with re.IGNORECASE).
   Pattern matching should be fast — this may be called on every tool error.

7. The patterns list should be ordered by specificity — more specific patterns
   first, generic fallbacks last. translate_error returns on FIRST match.

8. No hou import at module level. get_error_context imports hou lazily.
   translate_error and translate_tool_error work without hou.

VERIFY:
- Run: python -c "
from synapse.panel.error_translator import translate_error, translate_tool_error
r = translate_error('Unable to read file /path/to/texture.exr')
print(r['explanation'])
print(r['suggestion'])
r2 = translate_tool_error('houdini_set_parm', 'VEX error: Syntax error, unexpected token')
print(r2)
print('Pattern count:', len(__import__('synapse.panel.error_translator', fromlist=['ERROR_PATTERNS']).ERROR_PATTERNS))
"

I need you to create a session journal for SYNAPSE.

CONTEXT:
- Repo root: C:\Users\User\SYNAPSE
- SYNAPSE runs inside Houdini 21
- Every tool execution and slash command should be logged automatically
- The journal is append-only, stored at $HIP/claude/journal.log
- Artists can search it with /journal, and it feeds into scene memory

YOUR TASK:
Create python/synapse/panel/session_journal.py

REQUIREMENTS:

1. Class SessionJournal:

   __init__(self, log_dir: str = "")
   - If log_dir empty, try to resolve from hou.hipFile.path() → dirname/claude/
   - If hou unavailable, use a temp directory
   - Create the log directory if it doesn't exist
   - Open/create journal.log file path (don't keep file handle open)
   - Store session start time

   log_tool(self, tool_name: str, tool_input: dict, result: Any, error: str = None, duration_ms: int = 0)
   - Logs a tool execution. Format:
     [HH:MM:SS] TOOL tool_name: brief_summary (duration_ms ms)
     Brief summary should be smart — not dump the whole input dict, but extract
     the key info:
     - create_node: "Created {type} at {path}"
     - set_parm: "Set {path}/{parm} = {value}"
     - connect_nodes: "Connected {src} → {dst}"
     - execute_python: "Ran Python snippet ({n} chars)"
     - For others: first 80 chars of JSON input

   log_command(self, command: str, result_summary: str = "")
   - Logs a slash command execution. Format:
     [HH:MM:SS] CMD {command}: {result_summary}

   log_event(self, event_type: str, message: str)
   - Generic event log. Format:
     [HH:MM:SS] {EVENT_TYPE} {message}
   - Used for: shot_login, diagnosis results, preflight results, errors

   search(self, query: str, limit: int = 50) -> list
   - Search journal entries matching the query string (case-insensitive).
   - Returns list of matching lines, most recent first.
   - If query is empty, returns the last `limit` entries.

   get_session_summary(self) -> str
   - Returns a brief summary of the current session:
     "Session: {duration}min, {tool_count} tools, {cmd_count} commands"
   - Reads from in-memory counters (don't re-parse the file).

   get_entries(self, limit: int = 50) -> list
   - Returns the last N entries from the journal file.
   - Reads from the file (not in-memory) for persistence across panel restarts.

2. Function format_journal_html(entries: list, query: str = "") -> str
   Formats journal entries as HTML for the panel's QTextEdit.
   - Monospace font for log entries
   - Highlight matching query terms in entries (bold or color)
   - Show entry count and any search query at the top
   - If query provided: "Found N entries matching '{query}'"
   - If no query: "Last N entries (session: {summary})"

3. Module-level singleton pattern:
   _journal_instance: Optional[SessionJournal] = None

   def get_journal(log_dir: str = "") -> SessionJournal:
       """Get or create the singleton journal instance."""
       global _journal_instance
       if _journal_instance is None:
           _journal_instance = SessionJournal(log_dir)
       return _journal_instance

4. File I/O:
   - Append to journal.log on each log call (open, append, close — don't keep handle)
   - Use encoding='utf-8' on all file operations
   - Each entry is a single line (no multi-line entries)
   - File format is plain text, one entry per line
   - Handle file I/O errors gracefully (log to stderr, don't crash)

5. In-memory counters:
   - self._tool_count: int = 0
   - self._cmd_count: int = 0
   - self._event_count: int = 0
   - self._start_time: float = time.time()
   Incremented on each log call. Used for get_session_summary().

6. Tool summarization — _summarize_tool(tool_name, tool_input, result, error):
   Returns a concise one-line summary. Pattern-match on common tool names:

   TOOL_SUMMARIES = {
       "houdini_create_node": lambda inp, res, err: f"Created {inp.get('type','')} at {inp.get('path','')}",
       "houdini_set_parm": lambda inp, res, err: f"Set {inp.get('path','')}/{inp.get('parm','')} = {inp.get('value','')}",
       "houdini_connect_nodes": lambda inp, res, err: f"Connected {inp.get('source','')} → {inp.get('destination','')}",
       "houdini_delete_node": lambda inp, res, err: f"Deleted {inp.get('path','')}",
       "houdini_execute_python": lambda inp, res, err: f"Ran Python ({len(inp.get('code',''))} chars)",
       "houdini_execute_vex": lambda inp, res, err: f"Ran VEX on {inp.get('node_path','')}",
       "houdini_render": lambda inp, res, err: f"Rendered {inp.get('rop_path','')}",
       "houdini_hda_package": lambda inp, res, err: f"Packaged HDA '{inp.get('name','')}'",
   }

   For unknown tools: truncate json.dumps(tool_input) to 80 chars.
   If error: append " [FAILED: {error[:60]}]"

7. hou import is try/excepted. Journal works without hou (uses provided log_dir or temp).

8. Thread safety: use a threading.Lock around file writes. The journal
   may be written from the main thread (tool executor) and read from
   the panel's UI thread.

VERIFY:
- Run: python -c "
from synapse.panel.session_journal import SessionJournal, get_journal, format_journal_html
j = SessionJournal()
j.log_tool('houdini_create_node', {'type': 'geo', 'path': '/obj'}, {'node_path': '/obj/geo1'})
j.log_command('/diagnose', 'Found 3 issues')
j.log_event('LOGIN', 'Shot login: project=flat, scene=flat')
entries = j.get_entries()
print(f'{len(entries)} entries')
print(entries[0])
print(j.get_session_summary())
html = format_journal_html(entries)
print(f'HTML length: {len(html)} chars')
"

   Each entry:
   {
